t: Learn Through Play

c.b:
Om Namah Shri Acharya Vardhamansagaraya
A few years ago, scriptural study (shastra swadhyaya) used to take place regularly in Jina temples in the evenings. But nowadays, in this age of material pursuits, dazzled by worldly means, no one has time for such study. Whatever little study does happen is usually confined only to Adhyatma (spirituality), Dravyanuyoga (the doctrine of substances), and the Nishchaya-naya (the absolute standpoint) — leaving people unacquainted with the other subjects of the Agam.
We present in your hands this small book, "Gagar Mein Sagar" ("An Ocean in a Pot"). It brings together a very good collection of short question-and-answer sets covering almost all the Anuyogas (branches of scriptural exposition). This book will help everyone gain knowledge — from small children to the elderly.
Through this book, religious-minded people of every group can acquire knowledge of the Agam while playing games.
Any brothers and sisters who wish to take part and play these games should be given this book a few days in advance to memorize, so that they can properly remember the answers to its questions. Before that, let them know in advance which topics the questions will be drawn from. Give children topics suited to children, and give the more learned participants topics suited to them. Then begin the game on a fixed date.
1. Cricket: Form two teams of 11 players each. One player "bowls" six balls to the opposing "batsman" — that is, asks six questions. If the batsman answers within 5 seconds, it counts as six runs. If he answers between 5 and 10 seconds, it counts as four runs. In this way you may fix the run-values (1 run, 2 runs, etc.) as convenient. If the opposing player cannot answer within the fixed time, he is given out. In this way you can have fun while playing this game.
2. Antakshari: Form teams of 5 each, or as convenient, and form groups. An Antakshari-style contest is then held among them, as is done in World Cup-style formats for other games, and whoever wins the final round is declared the winner.
3. Written Examination: Here you may have candidates fill out a form for whichever examination they wish to take, give them the book, and then hold a written examination at a fixed time. The examiner may prepare the question paper as they see fit, leaving space after each question for the answer to be written in. You may allot 95 marks for the paper and 5 marks for neatness and cleanliness, etc., so as to make it easier to declare first, second place, and so on.
Other similar games may also be played in the same way.

t: ** Write the Namokar Mantra.

c.b: ** Write the Namokar Mantra.
: Namo Arihantanam, Namo Siddhanam, Namo Airiyanam, Namo Uvajjhayanam, Namo Loe Savva-sahunam.

t: ** Write the greatness (mahatmya) of the Namokar Mantra, along with its meaning.

c.b: ** Write the greatness (mahatmya) of the Namokar Mantra, along with its meaning.

: Eso Pancha Namokaro, Savva Pavappanasano; Mangalanam Cha Savvesim, Padhamam Hoi Mangalam.
(Translation: This five-fold obeisance destroys all sin; and among all auspicious things, it is the very first auspicious thing.) This five-fold obeisance mantra — the Namokar Mantra — destroys all the sins committed by us, and it is the foremost among all auspicious things (mangalas).

t: ** Who composed the Namokar Mantra?

c.b: ** Who composed the Namokar Mantra?
: In terms of its underlying meaning (bhava), the Namokar Mantra is beginningless and endless (anadi-nidhan, without origin or end). No one composed it.

t: ** Who first wrote it down, and where?

c.b: ** Who first wrote it down, and where?
: It was first written down as the mangalacharan (opening auspicious invocation) of the Shatkhandagama, by Acharya Shri Pushpadanta ji and Bhutabali ji.

t: ** In which language, and in which meter, is the Namokar Mantra composed?

c.b: ** In which language, and in which meter, is the Namokar Mantra composed?
: It is in the Prakrit language, in the gatha meter.

t: ** Give the meaning of the Namokar Mantra.

c.b: ** Give the meaning of the Namokar Mantra.

: Obeisance to the Arihants (Arihant, the Worthy Victor who has destroyed the four destructive/ghati karmas). Obeisance to the Siddhas (Siddha, the fully Liberated Souls). Obeisance to the Acharyas (Acharya, the head-preceptors of the monastic order). Obeisance to the Upadhyayas (Upadhyaya, the teacher-preceptors). Obeisance to all the Sadhus (Sadhu, monks) that exist anywhere in the world.

t: ** What other readings of "Arihant" are found?

c.b: ** What other readings of "Arihant" are found?
: In the Sapta Smarana (the Seven Recollections) three readings are given — (1) Arahantanam (2) Arihantanam (3) Aruhantanam. Ancient handwritten manuscripts also contain the reading "Ahamtanam."

t: ** Are the other readings incorrect?

c.b: ** Are the other readings incorrect?
: No — in all of them the word is derived from "Arhat" (the Worthy One). Hence all of them are correct.

t: ** What is the meaning of "Aruhantanam"?

c.b: ** What is the meaning of "Aruhantanam"?
: One who is not reborn. That is, because the seed of karma has been burnt away, those for whom rebirth no longer occurs are called Aruhantanam.

t: ** How is "Arahantanam" a correct reading?

c.b: ** How is "Arahantanam" a correct reading?
: Because they are supremely worshipped by the gods (devas), they are called Arahant or Arhant.

t: ** What is the meaning of "Arihantanam"?

c.b: ** What is the meaning of "Arihantanam"?
: "Ari" means enemy. Hence those who have destroyed (kshaya) the enemy in the form of karma — the ghati (destructive) karmas — are called Arihant.

t: ** Explain how the syllable Om (ॐ) is contained within the Namokar Mantra.

c.b: ** Explain how the syllable Om (ॐ) is contained within the Namokar Mantra.

: The "अ" (a) of Arihant, the "अ" (a) of Siddha (the bodiless one), the "आ" (aa) of Acharya, the "उ" (u) of Upadhyaya, and the "म" (m) of Muni [combine as follows]: a + a = aa; aa + u = o; o + m = Om (ॐ).

t: ** To whom is obeisance offered in the Namokar Mantra?

c.b: ** To whom is obeisance offered in the Namokar Mantra?
: In the Namokar Mantra, obeisance is offered to the Panch Parameshthi (the Five Supreme Beings).

t: ** Who are the Panch Parameshthi?

c.b: ** Who are the Panch Parameshthi?
: Arihant, Siddha, Acharya, Upadhyaya, and all Sadhus.

t: ** Who is called a Parameshthi?

c.b: ** Who is called a Parameshthi?
: One who is established in the supreme state (param pad) is called a Parameshthi (one abiding in the Supreme Station).

t: ** Who is called Arihant Parameshthi?

c.b: ** Who is called Arihant Parameshthi?
: Those who have destroyed the four ghati (destructive) karmas and who have attained the Ananta Chatushtaya (the Four Infinitudes) are called Arihant.

t: ** Who is called Siddha Parameshthi?

c.b: ** Who is called Siddha Parameshthi?

: Those who have become forever free of dravya karma (material karma), bhava karma (psychic karma), and no-karma (the body and other quasi-karmic matter), and who have attained the wealth of liberation (moksha-lakshmi), are called Siddha Parameshthi.

t: ** Who is called Acharya Parameshthi?

c.b: ** Who is called Acharya Parameshthi?

: Those who bear the 36 fundamental virtues (mula-gunas) and who direct the order of monks (muni-sangha), and who confer initiation (diksha), instruction (shiksha), and atonement/penance (prayashchitta).

t: ** Who is called Upadhyaya Parameshthi?

c.b: ** Who is called Upadhyaya Parameshthi?
: Those who study and teach the scriptures within the order of monks.

t: ** Who is called Sadhu Parameshthi?

c.b: ** Who is called Sadhu Parameshthi?
: Those who remain constantly absorbed in knowledge, meditation, and austerity (tapa).

t: ** How many fundamental virtues (mula-guna) does the Arihant Parameshthi have? List them separately.

c.b: ** How many fundamental virtues (mula-guna) does the Arihant Parameshthi have? List them separately.

: There are 46 fundamental virtues — 36 marvels (atishaya), comprising 10 of birth, 10 of Kevalgyan (omniscience), and 14 wrought by the gods; together with the 8 divine accompaniments (pratiharya); and the 4 infinitudes (ananta chatushtaya).

t: ** Name the ten marvels (atishaya) of birth.

c.b: ** Name the ten marvels (atishaya) of birth.

: 1. the absence of urine and excrement, 2. white blood, 3. a beautiful form, 4. incomparable strength, 5. a perfectly symmetrical body (samachaturasra-samsthana), 6. the adamantine bone-and-joint structure (vajra-vrishabha-naracha-samhanan), 7. speech that is beneficial, measured, and pleasant, 8. a naturally fragrant body, 9. a body free of fatigue, 10. one thousand and eight auspicious marks on the body.

t: ** Name the ten marvels (atishaya) of Kevalgyan (omniscience).

c.b: ** Name the ten marvels (atishaya) of Kevalgyan (omniscience).

: (1) abundant food within a hundred yojanas in all four directions, (2) the power to move through the sky, (3) no longer needing to take mouthfuls of food, (4) freedom from all adversity/affliction (upsarga), (5) the face appearing visible from all four directions, (6) the nails and hair no longer growing, (7) a shadowless body, (8) the eyelids no longer blinking, (9) no harm coming to any living being nearby (a state of compassion/non-violence), (10) mastery over all forms of knowledge and skill.

t: ** Name the 14 marvels wrought by the gods (devakrita atishaya).

c.b: ** Name the 14 marvels wrought by the gods (devakrita atishaya).

: 1. all beings understanding [the divine speech] in their own language, 2. a spirit of universal amity among all, 3. the fruits and flowers of every season blossoming together, 4. the ground becoming mirror-smooth and level, 5. a gentle, fragrant breeze, 6. the absence of plague and calamity (a state of universal supreme bliss), 7. the ground becoming free of dust and thorns, 8. a shower of scented water, 9. a clear, cloudless sky, 10. golden lotuses arising beneath each footstep, 11. the earth becoming filled with wealth and grain, 12. the Dharma-chakra (wheel of the Law) moving before him, 13. cries of victory resounding in the sky, 14. the eight auspicious substances (ashta-mangala-dravya).

t: ** What are the eight divine accompaniments (ashta-pratiharya)?

c.b: ** What are the eight divine accompaniments (ashta-pratiharya)?

: 1. the Ashoka tree, 2. a rain of celestial flowers, 3. the lion-throne (simhasana), 4. the sixty-four fly-whisks (chamara), 5. the triple canopy (three chhatra), 6. the divine sound/speech (divya-dhvani), 7. the divine kettle-drums (devadundubhi), 8. the halo of light (prabhamandala).

t: ** What are the four infinitudes (ananta chatushtaya)?

c.b: ** What are the four infinitudes (ananta chatushtaya)?
: 1. Anantajnana (infinite knowledge) 2. Anantadarshan (infinite perception) 3. Anantasukha (infinite bliss) 4. Anantavirya (infinite power).

t: ** How many of the Arihant Parameshthi's virtues belong to the soul, and how many belong to the body?

c.b: ** How many of the Arihant Parameshthi's virtues belong to the soul, and how many belong to the body?
: The four infinitudes belong to the soul, and the remaining 42 virtues are body-based.

t: ** Through the absence of which karmas do the four infinitudes manifest?

c.b: ** Through the absence of which karmas do the four infinitudes manifest?

: Through the destruction of jnanavaraniya karma (knowledge-obscuring karma), infinite knowledge; through the destruction of darshanavaraniya karma (perception-obscuring karma), infinite perception; through the destruction of mohaniya karma (deluding karma), infinite bliss; through the destruction of antaraya karma (obstructing karma), infinite power.

t: ** How many karmic states does the Arihant destroy?

c.b: ** How many karmic states does the Arihant destroy?
: 63 subsidiary karmic states (uttara-prakriti).

t: ** What are these 63 states?

c.b: ** What are these 63 states?
: 47 belonging to the ghati (destructive) karmas, 13 belonging to nama karma (body-determining karma), and 3 belonging to ayu karma (life-span karma).

t: ** What are the 13 states of nama karma?

c.b: ** What are the 13 states of nama karma?

: hell-destiny, the transmigratory-link to hell-destiny, animal-destiny, the transmigratory-link to animal-destiny, the "three incompletenesses" (viklatraya: two-sensed, three-sensed, and four-sensed embodiment), one-sensed embodiment, bioluminescence (udyota), heat-body (atapa), subtle body (sukshma), common/undifferentiated body (sadharana), and immobility (sthavara).

t: ** Which three life-spans (ayu) does an Arihant never have?

c.b: ** Which three life-spans (ayu) does an Arihant never have?
: hell-life-span, animal-life-span, and celestial-life-span.

t: ** How many fundamental virtues does the Siddha Parameshthi have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many fundamental virtues does the Siddha Parameshthi have? Name them.

: There are eight fundamental virtues — infinite knowledge, infinite perception, the destruction-based right faith (kshayika samyaktva), infinite power, the state of occupying a fixed measure of space (avagahanatva), subtleness (sukshmatva), imperturbability (avyabadhatva), and weightless-buoyancy (agurulaghutva).

t: ** Through the absence of which karmas do the Siddha's eight virtues manifest?

c.b: ** Through the absence of which karmas do the Siddha's eight virtues manifest?

: Through jnanavaraniya karma, infinite knowledge; through darshanavaraniya karma, infinite perception; through mohaniya karma, destruction-based right faith; through antaraya karma, infinite power; through nama karma, subtleness; through ayu karma, the fixed-space-occupying quality; through gotra karma (status-determining karma), weightless-buoyancy; and through vedaniya karma (feeling-producing karma), imperturbability.

t: ** How many fundamental virtues does the Acharya Parameshthi have? What are they?

c.b: ** How many fundamental virtues does the Acharya Parameshthi have? What are they?

: The Acharya Parameshthi has 36 fundamental virtues — 10 dharmas (virtues), 12 austerities (tapa), the 5 branches of right conduct (panchachara), the 6 essential duties (avashyaka), and the 3 restraints (gupti).

t: ** Name the ten dharmas (dasha-dharma).

c.b: ** Name the ten dharmas (dasha-dharma).

: supreme forgiveness (uttama-kshama), humility (mardava), straightforwardness (arjava), truthfulness (satya), contentment/purity (shaucha), self-restraint (sanyama), austerity (tapa), renunciation (tyaga), non-attachment (akinchanya), and celibacy (brahmacharya).

t: ** What are the twelve austerities (barah tapa)?

c.b: ** What are the twelve austerities (barah tapa)?
: six external (bahya) and six internal (abhyantar).

t: ** What are the six external austerities?

c.b: ** What are the six external austerities?

: fasting (anashan), reduced diet (avamaudarya), restriction of the range of alms accepted (vritti-parisankhyana), dwelling in a solitary spot (vivikta-shayyasana), giving up rich or flavorful food (rasa-parityaga), and mortification of the body (kayaklesha).

t: ** What are the six internal austerities?

c.b: ** What are the six internal austerities?
: atonement (prayashchitta), reverence (vinaya), service to fellow ascetics (vaiyavritya), scriptural study (svadhyaya), the letting-go of attachment to the body (vyutsarga), and meditation (dhyana).

t: ** What are the five branches of right conduct (panchachara)?

c.b: ** What are the five branches of right conduct (panchachara)?
: right-faith conduct (darshanachara), right-knowledge conduct (jnanachara), right-character conduct (charitrachara), austerity conduct (tapachara), and energy conduct (viryachara).

t: ** What are the six essential duties (avashyaka) of an Acharya?

c.b: ** What are the six essential duties (avashyaka) of an Acharya?

: equanimity practice (samayika), praise of the twenty-four Tirthankaras (chaturvimshati-stavana), veneration (vandana), repentance (pratikramana), the vow of renunciation (pratyakhyana), and bodily abandonment in meditation (kayotsarga).

t: ** What are the three restraints (gupti)?

c.b: ** What are the three restraints (gupti)?
: restraint of mind (mano-gupti), restraint of speech (vachana-gupti), and restraint of body (kaya-gupti).

t: ** How many fundamental virtues does the Upadhyaya Parameshthi have?

c.b: ** How many fundamental virtues does the Upadhyaya Parameshthi have?
: 25 fundamental virtues — the eleven Angas (primary scriptural limbs) and the fourteen Purvas (ancient scriptural texts).

t: ** How many fundamental virtues does the Sadhu Parameshthi have?

c.b: ** How many fundamental virtues does the Sadhu Parameshthi have?
: 28 fundamental virtues — the five great vows (mahavrata), the five carefulnesses (samiti), the restraint of the five senses, the six essential duties, and seven other remaining virtues.

t: ** What are the five great vows (panch mahavrata)?

c.b: ** What are the five great vows (panch mahavrata)?
: non-violence (ahimsa), truthfulness (satya), non-stealing (achaurya), celibacy (brahmacharya), and non-possession (aparigraha).

t: ** Name the five carefulnesses (samiti).

c.b: ** Name the five carefulnesses (samiti).
: care in walking (irya), care in speech (bhasha), care in seeking food (eshana), care in picking up and setting down objects (adana-nikshepana), and care in the disposal of waste (pratishthapana).

t: ** What are the other seven virtues?

c.b: ** What are the other seven virtues?

: plucking out one's own hair (keshalunchana), not bathing (asnana), sleeping on the bare ground (bhumishayana), not brushing the teeth [with any instrument] (adantadhavana), eating while standing (khade-khade bhojana), nakedness (nagnatva), and eating only once a day.

t: ** How many syllables does the Namokar Mantra have?

c.b: ** How many syllables does the Namokar Mantra have?
: 35 syllables — Namo Arihantanam: 7, Namo Siddhanam: 5, Namo Airiyanam: 7, Namo Uvajjhayanam: 7, Namo Loe Savva-sahunam: 9. (7+5+7+7+9=35.)

t: ** How many lines (pada) does the Namokar Mantra have?

c.b: ** How many lines (pada) does the Namokar Mantra have?
: Five lines — 1. Namo Arihantanam, 2. Namo Siddhanam, 3. Namo Airiyanam, 4. Namo Uvajjhayanam, 5. Namo Loe Savva-sahunam.

t: ** Which Parameshthis can possess the four kinds of knowledge?

c.b: ** Which Parameshthis can possess the four kinds of knowledge?
: Three Parameshthis — Acharya, Upadhyaya, and Sadhu.

t: ** Which Parameshthi is certain to attain liberation in this very life?

c.b: ** Which Parameshthi is certain to attain liberation in this very life?
: The Arihant Parameshthi alone.

t: ** Which Parameshthis make use of the senses and the mind, and engage in deliberative thought?

c.b: ** Which Parameshthis make use of the senses and the mind, and engage in deliberative thought?
: Three Parameshthis — Acharya, Upadhyaya, and Sadhu Parameshthi.

t: ** Which Parameshthis are free of the passions (kashaya)?

c.b: ** Which Parameshthis are free of the passions (kashaya)?
: Arihant and Siddha Parameshthi.

t: ** Which Parameshthis are free of both karma and body?

c.b: ** Which Parameshthis are free of both karma and body?
: The Siddha Parameshthi alone.

t: ** Which Parameshthis practise the plucking out of hair (keshalunchana)?

c.b: ** Which Parameshthis practise the plucking out of hair (keshalunchana)?
: Acharya, Upadhyaya, and Sadhu — three.

t: ** Which Parameshthis wander [from place to place]?

c.b: ** Which Parameshthis wander [from place to place]?
: Arihant, Acharya, Upadhyaya, and Sadhu — these four Parameshthis wander.

t: ** Which Parameshthis do not keep a pichi (peacock-feather whisk) and kamandalu (water-pot)?

c.b: ** Which Parameshthis do not keep a pichi (peacock-feather whisk) and kamandalu (water-pot)?
: Two Parameshthis — Arihant and Siddha.

t: ** How many syllables of the Panch Parameshthi's names can be used for japa (recitation) and dhyana (meditation)?

c.b: ** How many syllables of the Panch Parameshthi's names can be used for japa (recitation) and dhyana (meditation)?
: Thirty-five, sixteen, six, five, four, two, and one syllable can be used for japa and dhyana.

t: ** What is the sixteen-syllable mantra?

c.b: ** What is the sixteen-syllable mantra?

: Arihanta-Siddha-Airiya-Uvajjhaya-Sahu, or: Namah Arhat-Siddhacharya-Upadhyaya-Sarva-Sadhubhyah.
(Translation: Obeisance to the Arihant, the Siddha, the Acharya, the Upadhyaya, and to all the Sadhus.)

t: ** What is the six-syllable mantra?

c.b: ** What is the six-syllable mantra?

: Arihant, Siddha. Arihant Sisa [Siddha]. Om Namah Siddhebhyah. Namo'rha Siddhebhyah.
(Translation: Om, obeisance to the Siddhas; obeisance to the Worthy Siddhas.)

t: ** What are the five-syllable mantras?

c.b: ** What are the five-syllable mantras?
: A Si Aa U Sa [the seed-syllables for Arihant-Siddha-Acharya-Upadhyaya-Sadhu]. Namo Siddhanam (Obeisance to the Siddhas).

t: ** What are the four-syllable mantras?

c.b: ** What are the four-syllable mantras?
: Arihant. A Si Sahum.

t: ** What is the seven-syllable mantra?

c.b: ** What is the seven-syllable mantra?
: Om Hrim Shrim Arha Namah. A Si Aa U Sa Namah.

t: ** What is the eight-syllable mantra?

c.b: ** What is the eight-syllable mantra?
: Om Namo Arihantanam (Om, obeisance to the Arihants).

t: ** What is the two-syllable mantra?

c.b: ** What is the two-syllable mantra?
: Om Hrim. Siddha. A Si.

t: ** What is the one-syllable mantra?

c.b: ** What is the one-syllable mantra?
: Om. Hrim.

t: ** What is the thirteen-syllable mantra?

c.b: ** What is the thirteen-syllable mantra?
: (1) Om Arhat Siddha Sayoga-Kevali Svaha. (2) Om Haam Hreem Hoom Haum Hah A Si Aa U Sa Namah.

t: ** How many kinds of Kevali (omniscient beings) are there? What are they?

c.b: ** How many kinds of Kevali (omniscient beings) are there? What are they?

: Seven kinds — (1) Tirthankara-Kevali (2) Samanya-Kevali (ordinary Kevali) (3) Upasarga-Kevali (afflicted Kevali) (4) Muka-Kevali (silent Kevali) (5) Antakrit-Kevali (Kevali who attains liberation at the very moment of omniscience) (6) Samudghata-Kevali (Kevali who performs the karmic dispersion) (7) Anubaddha-Kevali (Kevali who arises in unbroken succession).

t: ** Give the definition of each kind of Kevali.

c.b: ** Give the definition of each kind of Kevali.

:
1. Tirthankara-Kevali — one in whom the tirthankara-nama-karma (the karma of Ford-Making) comes to fruition; whose preaching hall (samavasarana) is built; who has [the remaining] auspicious life-events (kalyanaka); and from whose presence the divine sound (divya-dhvani) issues.
2. Samanya Kevali (ordinary Kevali) — one who becomes a Kevali simply by destroying the four ghati (destructive) karmas, without such special marks; for whom a fragrance-hall (gandha-kuti) is built, and who also delivers religious discourse — for example, Rama and Hanuman.
3. Upasarga-Kevali — one to whom omniscience (kevalgyan) arises in the midst of an affliction (upasarga), and who also delivers religious discourse — for example, Kulabhushana and Deshabhushana.
4. Muka-Kevali (silent Kevali) — one whose speech does not resound (i.e. who does not give discourse) even after attaining omniscience.
5. Antakrit-Kevali — one to whom omniscience arises either through a terrible affliction or in the ordinary course, and who, at that very moment, destroys all eight karmas and attains liberation — for example, the three Pandavas.
6. Samudghata-Kevali — when the duration of the nama (body-determining), gotra (status-determining), and vedaniya (feeling-producing) karmas exceeds that of the ayu (life-span) karma, a Sayoga-Kevali (an omniscient being still possessing activity) performs the karmic dispersion (samudghata) at the final moment in order to equalize their duration with that of the ayu karma; such a one is called a Samudghata-Kevali.
7. Anubaddha-Kevali — those Kevalis who arise in unbroken succession, such that as soon as one attains liberation, the next attains omniscience, and when that one in turn attains liberation, a third attains omniscience, and so on in sequence.

t: ** Who is called a Tirthankara?

c.b: ** Who is called a Tirthankara?

: 1. One who sets the ford of religion (dharma-tirtha) in motion. 2. One who crosses [the ocean of worldly existence] himself and shows others the path to cross the ocean of transmigration. 3. One whose auspicious life-events (kalyanaka) occur, and whose divine preaching-hall (samavasarana) is built. 4. One who gives the true teaching of religion — such a one is called a Tirthankara.

t: ** How many chief disciples (ganadhara) did all twenty-four Tirthankaras have in total?

c.b: ** How many chief disciples (ganadhara) did all twenty-four Tirthankaras have in total?
: 1,459 ganadharas.

t: ** Why, when, and how — and by whom — is a Tirthankara's emblem determined?

c.b: ** Why, when, and how — and by whom — is a Tirthankara's emblem determined?

: A Tirthankara is identified by his emblem. At the time of the birth-kalyanaka (auspicious birth-event), atop Mount Sumeru, the emblem that appears on the right big toe of Lord [the infant Tirthankara] as [placed before] Saudharma Indra determines the emblem accordingly.

t: ** What is meant by a kalyanaka (auspicious event)? How many are there? Name them.

c.b: ** What is meant by a kalyanaka (auspicious event)? How many are there? Name them.

: The occasions on which the gods hold celebrations for the sake of a Tirthankara are called kalyanaka. There are five: 1. conception (garbha) 2. birth (janma) 3. renunciation/austerity (tapa) 4. omniscience (kevalgyan) 5. liberation (moksha).

t: ** Is it necessary that every Tirthankara have all five kalyanakas?

c.b: ** Is it necessary that every Tirthankara have all five kalyanakas?
: The Tirthankaras of the Bharat and Airavat regions always have all five kalyanakas. But the Tirthankaras of the Videha region may have two, three, or five kalyanakas.

t: ** For whom are there [only] two kalyanakas?

c.b: ** For whom are there [only] two kalyanakas?

: For one who first takes renunciation (diksha) and only afterward binds the tirthankara-nama-karma, and who attains liberation in that same life — for such a one, only the omniscience (jnana) and liberation (moksha) kalyanakas occur.

t: ** How would there be three kalyanakas?

c.b: ** How would there be three kalyanakas?

: For one who will attain liberation in that same life, but who did not take renunciation [before binding the tirthankara-karma] — having bound the tirthankara-nama-karma in this very life — his kalyanakas will be renunciation (tapa), omniscience (jnana), and liberation (moksha).

t: ** At most, how many Tirthankaras can there be at one and the same time?

c.b: ** At most, how many Tirthankaras can there be at one and the same time?
: At any one time, there can be at most 170 Tirthankaras.

t: ** How can there be 170 at once?

c.b: ** How can there be 170 at once?

: In relation to one Mount Sumeru there are one Bharat, one Airavat, and 32 Videha regions [each capable of having a Tirthankara]. In this way, across the five Merus, 34 × 5 = 170 Tirthankaras can exist.

t: ** At the very least, how many Tirthankaras can there be at one time?

c.b: ** At the very least, how many Tirthankaras can there be at one time?
: There are [at least] 20 Tirthankaras.

t: ** Are there Tirthankaras existing right now? If so, where?

c.b: ** Are there Tirthankaras existing right now? If so, where?
: Yes — at present, there are 20 Tirthankaras in the Videha regions belonging to the five Merus.

t: ** At present, how many Tirthankaras are there in Jambudvipa? Name them.

c.b: ** At present, how many Tirthankaras are there in Jambudvipa? Name them.
: Simandhar, Yugamandhar, Bahu, and Subahu are the four Tirthankaras.

t: ** In Dhatakikhanda, which Tirthankaras belong to Vijaya-meru?

c.b: ** In Dhatakikhanda, which Tirthankaras belong to Vijaya-meru?
: Sanjata, Svayamprabha, Rishabhanana, and Anantavirya — these four.

t: ** In Dhatakikhanda, which Tirthankaras belong to Achala-meru?

c.b: ** In Dhatakikhanda, which Tirthankaras belong to Achala-meru?
: Suriprabha, Vishalkirti, Vajradhar, and Chandranana — these four.

t: ** In Pushkarardha-dvipa, which Tirthankaras belong to Mandara-meru?

c.b: ** In Pushkarardha-dvipa, which Tirthankaras belong to Mandara-meru?
: Bhadrabahu, Bhujangam, Ishwar, and Nemiprabh — these four.

t: ** In Pushkarardha-dvipa, name the Tirthankaras belonging to Vidyunmali-meru.

c.b: ** In Pushkarardha-dvipa, name the Tirthankaras belonging to Vidyunmali-meru.
: Virasen, Mahabhadra, Devayash, and Ajitavirya — these four.

t: ** How many Tirthankaras of the present set of twenty-four observed lifelong celibacy from childhood (bal-brahmachari)? Name them.

c.b: ** How many Tirthankaras of the present set of twenty-four observed lifelong celibacy from childhood (bal-brahmachari)? Name them.
: Five Tirthankaras — Vasupujya, Mallinath, Neminath, Parshvanath, and Lord Mahavir.

t: ** How many Tirthankaras held three offices/stations? Name them.

c.b: ** How many Tirthankaras held three offices/stations? Name them.
: Three Tirthankaras — Shantinath, Kunthunath, and Aranath [who were also Chakravartis, universal emperors, in addition to being Tirthankaras].

t: ** How many Tirthankaras had an affliction (upasarga) inflicted upon them?

c.b: ** How many Tirthankaras had an affliction (upasarga) inflicted upon them?
: Three Tirthankaras — Suparshvanath, Parshvanath, and Lord Mahavir.

t: ** After taking renunciation, which Tirthankara attained omniscience in the shortest time?

c.b: ** After taking renunciation, which Tirthankara attained omniscience in the shortest time?
: Mallinath ji, six days after taking renunciation.

t: ** After taking renunciation, which Tirthankara attained omniscience after the longest time?

c.b: ** After taking renunciation, which Tirthankara attained omniscience after the longest time?
: Lord Adinath, one thousand years after taking renunciation.

t: ** By how many, and which, Indras is the Lord Arihant worshipped?

c.b: ** By how many, and which, Indras is the Lord Arihant worshipped?

: He is venerated by 100 Indras — 40 of the Bhavanavasi [demigods], 32 of the Vyantaras, 24 of the Kalpavasis, 2 of the Jyotishas (the sun and moon), and among humans, the Chakravarti [universal emperor], and among animals, the lion. (40+32+24+2+1+1=100.)

t: ** In which time-period (kala) do the 24 Tirthankaras of the Bharat and Airavat regions occur?

c.b: ** In which time-period (kala) do the 24 Tirthankaras of the Bharat and Airavat regions occur?
: In the fourth time-period, Dushama-Sushama.

t: ** Did the ford of religion (dharma-tirtha) continue unbroken throughout the fourth time-period, or was there ever a break?

c.b: ** Did the ford of religion (dharma-tirtha) continue unbroken throughout the fourth time-period, or was there ever a break?
: There were breaks (vyucchitti) in the tirtha-period between seven Tirthankaras, from Pushpadanta to Dharmanath.

t: ** How long was the break during the era of each of these Tirthankaras?

c.b: ** How long was the break during the era of each of these Tirthankaras?

: In Shri Pushpadanta ji's era, a quarter of a palya; in Shri Shitalnath ji's era, half a palya; in Shri Shreyansanath ji's era, three-quarters of a palya; in Shri Vasupujya ji's era, a full palya; in Shri Vimalnath ji's era, three-quarters of a palya; in Shri Anantanath ji's era, half a palya; and in Shri Dharmanath ji's era, a quarter of a palya. (A palya is an immense unit of time.)

t: ** Did all the Tirthankaras appear only in the fourth time-period?

c.b: ** Did all the Tirthankaras appear only in the fourth time-period?
: No — Lord Adinath was born in the third time-period, and attained liberation in the third time-period itself.

t: ** Why do we take the darshan (auspicious sight) of the Lord?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** Why do we take the darshan (auspicious sight) of the Lord?

: The Jinendra Deva (the Victorious Lord) is free of the eighteen faults and possesses infinite virtues. We take his darshan in order to attain those virtues, and through it right faith (samyagdarshan) is also attained.

t: ** Why is it necessary to bathe before coming to the temple?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** Why is it necessary to bathe before coming to the temple?

: In household life, there are constantly five sources of subtle violence (pancha-suna) — the grindstone, the hearth, the mortar, the broom, and the place for filtering/discarding water — through which the body becomes impure. Hence bathing is necessary to purify the body.

t: ** Why should the feet be washed on entering the temple?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** Why should the feet be washed on entering the temple?

: The feet are directly connected to the mind. If the feet remain unclean, the mind too will remain unclean, and our dirty feet would also make the temple impure. Therefore one should wash the feet before entering the temple.

t: ** Why is rice specifically offered in the temple?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** Why is rice specifically offered in the temple?
: Because once the husk is removed, a grain of rice cannot sprout again; hence [we offer rice as a wish] that hereafter I too may not sprout again — that is, may not be reborn.

t: ** To whom is circumambulation (pradakshina) offered, and how many times?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** To whom is circumambulation (pradakshina) offered, and how many times?

: Three circumambulations are offered — to the passion-free Lords (vitaraga-deva), to the tirtha-kshetras (sites of the fords), to the siddha-kshetras (sites of liberation), to the atishaya-kshetras (sites of miraculous power), and to the unattached teachers — the munis, gurus, and aryikas (nuns).

t: ** On entering the temple, why should one say "Nissahi, Nissahi"?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** On entering the temple, why should one say "Nissahi, Nissahi"?
: If some deity (unseen) or some lay devotee is engaged in darshan there, may they grant me a place to also take darshan.

t: ** On leaving, why does one say "Assahi, Assahi"?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** On leaving, why does one say "Assahi, Assahi"?
: [To convey:] I have finished taking darshan and am now leaving; may whoever gave me this place now reclaim their place.

t: ** Why is a bell rung in the temple?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** Why is a bell rung in the temple?
: Its auspicious sound removes our mental pollution.

t: ** What is the benefit of ringing the bell?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** What is the benefit of ringing the bell?

: The sound of the conch and the bell destroys disease-causing germs. In Africa, the bell is rung to draw out the poison after a venomous snake-bite; in Moscow, tuberculosis is treated by ringing a bell. (As stated in the original text.)

t: ** With how many substances is puja (worship) performed? Name them.
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** With how many substances is puja (worship) performed? Name them.
: Puja is performed with the eight substances (ashta-dravya) — water, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains (akshata), flowers, food-offering (naivedya), lamp (deepa), incense (dhoopa), and fruit.

t: ** Why should puja be performed?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** Why should puja be performed?
: Puja is the foremost essential duty of a householder.

t: ** How many limbs (anga) does puja have?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** How many limbs (anga) does puja have?

: It has six limbs — abhisheka (ceremonial bathing of the image), ahvanana (invocation), sthapana (establishing [the deity's presence]), sannidhikarana (drawing near), worship with the eight substances, and visarjana (taking leave).

t: ** How should one go to the temple?
grp: 3. Deva-Darshan and Chaityalaya (Temple Visit and the Jina-Temple)

c.b: ** How should one go to the temple?
: One should never go to the temple empty-handed; one should take along some fruit and articles for worship.

c.b: ** What is meant by an akritrim chaityalaya (a "not man-made," naturally-arisen temple)?

: One that has not been built by any deity, vidyadhara (demigod-sorcerer), or human being; that has existed without beginning; that will remain in that same state for endless time; and in which an image of the Jina is enshrined.

t: ** What is meant by puja (worship)?

t: ** How many kinds of puja are there? Name them.

c.b: ** How many kinds of puja are there? Name them.
: Puja is of two kinds — dravya-puja (material worship) and bhava-puja (mental/inner worship).

t: ** What is meant by bhava-puja?

c.b: ** What is meant by bhava-puja?
: Reciting the virtues of the Lord without the use of material substances is bhava-puja.

t: ** Which mantra is recited while offering water?

c.b: ** Which mantra is recited while offering water?

: Om Hrim ... Janma-Jara-Mrityu-Vinashanaya Jalam Nirvapamiti Svaha.
(Translation: Om Hrim, I offer this water for the destruction of birth, old age, and death, svaha.)

c.b: ** Which mantra is recited while offering sandalwood paste?

c.b: ** Which mantra is recited while offering unbroken rice (akshata)?

t: ** Which mantra is recited while offering the argha (the combined final offering)?

t: ** Write out one argha-verse used in puja.

c.b: ** Write out one argha-verse used in puja.

: "Jala phala adhyam shuchisara tankon argha karon, tumako apon bhavatara bhavatari moksha varon. Chaubison Shri Jinachanda anandakanda sahi. Pad jajata harata bhavaphanda pavata mokshamahi." Om Hrim Shri Vrishabhadi Viranterbhyo Anargha-Pada-Praptaya Argha Nirvapamiti Svaha.
(Translation: With water and fruit, rich and pure, I offer you this argha; O ferry across worldly existence, grant me the boon of liberation. To all twenty-four Jina-lords, the very root of bliss, whose feet — when worshipped — destroy the snare of transmigration and bring one to the great land of liberation [I offer this]. Om Hrim, to the Lords from Rishabha to Mahavira, for the attainment of the priceless state, I offer this argha, svaha.)

t: ** Why is circumambulation (parikrama) performed in the temple?

c.b: ** Why is circumambulation (parikrama) performed in the temple?

: The temple is a symbol of the samavasarana (the divine preaching-hall), within which the Lord's face appears in all four directions at once. In order to take his darshan from every side, devotees perform circumambulation.

t: ** Which verse is recited while taking gandhodaka (the scented water used in temple ritual)?

c.b: ** Which verse is recited while taking gandhodaka (the scented water used in temple ritual)?

(Translation: I bow to the scented water of the Jina — that which is pure, which purifies, which is sacred, which destroys sin, and which destroys the eight karmas.)

: The word "pichhanya" means to recognize.

t: ** What are the various kinds of gods (deva) like?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** What are the various kinds of gods (deva) like?
: The various kinds of gods are sarāgī — still possessed of passion and attachment (unlike the passionless Jina).

t: ** In which forest has whose wealth been plundered by whom?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** In which forest has whose wealth been plundered by whom?
: In the terrible forest of worldly existence (bhava-vikatavana), my enemy in the form of karma has plundered the wealth that is knowledge.

t: ** Forgetting what, becoming what, have I wandered where?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** Forgetting what, becoming what, have I wandered where?
: Forgetting what is truly desirable (ishta) and becoming corrupted (bhrashta), I have wandered into what is undesirable — evil states of rebirth (durgati).

t: ** What all of mine has become blessed?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** What all of mine has become blessed?
: My hour has become blessed, my day has become blessed, and my very birth has become blessed.

t: ** For what reason did I attain the darshan (auspicious sight) of the Lord?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** For what reason did I attain the darshan (auspicious sight) of the Lord?
: I attained the Lord's darshan because of the rise of good fortune (bhagyodaya).

t: ** What are the Lord's countenance, posture, and gaze like?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** What are the Lord's countenance, posture, and gaze like?
: The Lord's countenance is vitaragi (free of passion), his posture is unclothed (digambara), and his gaze rests at the tip of his nose.

t: ** What is the meaning of the word "vasu"?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** What is the meaning of the word "vasu"?
: The word "vasu" means eight (8).

t: ** With how many qualities (gunas) is the Lord endowed?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** With how many qualities (gunas) is the Lord endowed?
: The Lord is endowed with infinite qualities.

t: ** Give the meaning of "koti ravi" and "timir."
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** Give the meaning of "koti ravi" and "timir."
: "Koti ravi" means crores of suns. "Timir" means darkness.

t: ** What was dispelled, and what arose?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** What was dispelled, and what arose?
: The darkness in the form of mithyatva (wrong belief) was dispelled, and the sun in the form of samyaktva (right belief) arose.

t: ** What is the meaning of "ur," and what happened in the ur?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** What is the meaning of "ur," and what happened in the ur?
: "Ur" means the heart, and joy arose in the heart.

t: ** Joining what, bowing what, out of what feeling, and where is he bowing?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** Joining what, bowing what, out of what feeling, and where is he bowing?
: Joining his two hands, bowing his head, out of reverence (vinaya), he is bowing at the feet of the Lord.

t: ** State the Lord's epithets.
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** State the Lord's epithets.

: Sarvatkrishta (the supreme, best of all), Trilokapati (Lord of the three worlds), Jina (the Victor), and Taran-taran (the one who ferries [beings] across [the ocean of transmigration]) are his epithets.

t: ** What is the devotee asking of the Lord?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** What is the devotee asking of the Lord?
: That he may attain devotion to the Lord birth after birth.

t: ** How many verses (chhand) are there in the "Prabhu Patitpavan" hymn of praise?
grp: 6. Prabhu Patit Pavan (The Lord, Redeemer of the Fallen)

c.b: ** How many verses (chhand) are there in the "Prabhu Patitpavan" hymn of praise?
: There are 8 verses in the "Prabhu Patitpavan" hymn of praise.

t: ** Who composed "Meri Bhavana"? How many verses does "Meri Bhavana" contain?

c.b: ** Who composed "Meri Bhavana"? How many verses does "Meri Bhavana" contain?
: "Meri Bhavana" was composed by Pandit Jugalkishor Mukhtar. "Meri Bhavana" contains 11 verses.

t: ** Describe vitaragata (passionlessness) as it appears in "Meri Bhavana."

c.b: ** Describe vitaragata (passionlessness) as it appears in "Meri Bhavana."
: Those who have conquered attachment (raga), aversion (dvesha), desire (kama), and the like, are vitaragi (passionless).

t: ** Describe sarvajnata (omniscience) as it appears in "Meri Bhavana."

c.b: ** Describe sarvajnata (omniscience) as it appears in "Meri Bhavana."
: They have known the whole universe; those who have known all substances of the loka (universe) and aloka (non-universe) are sarvajna (omniscient).

t: ** Describe hitopadeshita (the giving of beneficial teaching) as it appears in "Meri Bhavana."

c.b: ** Describe hitopadeshita (the giving of beneficial teaching) as it appears in "Meri Bhavana."
: They taught the path of liberation to all beings, desiring nothing for themselves.

t: ** Give the meaning of the word "nihsprih."

c.b: ** Give the meaning of the word "nihsprih."
: The word "nihsprih" means selflessness.

t: ** Name the synonyms of the Lord.

c.b: ** Name the synonyms of the Lord.
: Buddha, Vir, Jin, Hari, Har, and Brahma are synonyms of the Lord.

t: ** In what should my mind remain absorbed?

c.b: ** In what should my mind remain absorbed?
: Roused by devotion, may this mind remain ever absorbed in Him (the Arihant, the Siddha).

t: ** What is called vishaya (sense-object)?

c.b: ** What is called vishaya (sense-object)?
: That which is grasped through the senses is called vishaya.

t: ** What wealth do sadhus (monks) keep?

c.b: ** What wealth do sadhus (monks) keep?
: Sadhus keep the wealth of equanimity (samyabhav); sadhus keep the wealth that is samata (equanimity of mind).

t: ** In what, and when, are sadhus ever intent?

c.b: ** In what, and when, are sadhus ever intent?
: They are ever intent, day and night, on accomplishing the good of both self and others.

t: ** What kind of austerity do sadhus practice, and how?

c.b: ** What kind of austerity do sadhus practice, and how?
: They practise the difficult austerity of relinquishing self-interest, without any regret.

t: ** What do sadhus do for the world?

c.b: ** What do sadhus do for the world?
: They remove its mass of suffering. Sadhus remove the mass of suffering of the world.

t: ** With whom should there be constant company and constant contemplation?

c.b: ** With whom should there be constant company and constant contemplation?
: May there ever be the company of those sadhus who remove the mass of suffering, and may there ever be contemplation of them alone.

t: ** In what should my mind remain devoted?

c.b: ** In what should my mind remain devoted?
: May this mind remain ever devoted to conduct like that of the sadhus.

t: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of violence (hinsa).

c.b: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of violence (hinsa).
: May I never torment any living being; may I never torment any being at all.

t: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of falsehood (jhooth).

c.b: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of falsehood (jhooth).
: May I never speak an untruth; may I never utter falsehood.

t: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of theft (chori).

c.b: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of theft (chori).
: May I never be tempted by another's wealth or another's wife; may I never steal another's wealth, nor be infatuated with another's wife.

t: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of unchastity (kushil).

c.b: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of unchastity (kushil).
: May I never be tempted by another's spouse; may I never be tempted by another's wife.

t: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of possessiveness (parigraha) and the passion of greed (lobha-kashaya).

c.b: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the sin of possessiveness (parigraha) and the passion of greed (lobha-kashaya).
: May I drink the nectar of contentment; may I keep to contentment.

t: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the passion of pride (man-kashaya).

c.b: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the passion of pride (man-kashaya).
: May I hold no feeling of pride; may I never harbour a feeling of pride.

t: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the passion of deceit (maya-kashaya).

c.b: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the passion of deceit (maya-kashaya).
: May I deal simply and truthfully; may I deal in a straightforward manner.

t: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the passion of anger (krodh-kashaya).

c.b: ** State the aspiration for avoiding the passion of anger (krodh-kashaya).
: May I never be angry with anyone.

t: ** What should I do for others in this life?

c.b: ** What should I do for others in this life?
: As far as it is in my power, may I do good to others in this life.

t: ** What feeling should I bear toward all beings?

c.b: ** What feeling should I bear toward all beings?
: May I ever bear a feeling of friendship (maitri-bhava) toward all beings in the world.

t: ** Seeing wretched and suffering beings, what should flow in my heart?

c.b: ** Seeing wretched and suffering beings, what should flow in my heart?
: Seeing wretched and suffering beings, may a stream of compassion flow from my heart.

t: ** At what should I not feel resentment?

c.b: ** At what should I not feel resentment?
: May I not feel resentment toward the wicked, the cruel, and those set on the wrong path.

t: ** Toward what should I maintain equanimity (samyabhav)?

c.b: ** Toward what should I maintain equanimity (samyabhav)?
: May I maintain equanimity toward them — the wicked, the cruel, and those set on the wrong path.

t: ** Seeing virtuous people, what should well up in my heart?

c.b: ** Seeing virtuous people, what should well up in my heart?
: Seeing virtuous people, may love well up in my heart.

t: ** In serving whom should my mind find happiness?

c.b: ** In serving whom should my mind find happiness?
: As far as it is in my power, may this mind find happiness through serving them, the virtuous.

t: ** What should never enter my heart?

c.b: ** What should never enter my heart?
: May treachery never enter my heart.

t: ** What feeling should I always hold, in order to receive?

c.b: ** What feeling should I always hold, in order to receive?
: May I ever hold the disposition of recognizing others' virtues.

t: ** Toward what should my gaze never turn?

c.b: ** Toward what should my gaze never turn?
: May my gaze never turn toward others' faults.

t: ** Even if someone calls me good or bad, even if wealth comes or goes, even if I am tempted by fear, from what should I never waver?

c.b: ** Even if someone calls me good or bad, even if wealth comes or goes, even if I am tempted by fear, from what should I never waver?
: Even so, may my steps never waver from the path of justice.

t: ** In what should the mind not swell with pride, and in what should it not be distressed?

c.b: ** In what should the mind not swell with pride, and in what should it not be distressed?
: May it never swell with pride, exulting in happiness; may it never be distressed in suffering.

t: ** Of what should I not be afraid?

c.b: ** Of what should I not be afraid?
: May I not fear mountains, rivers, cremation grounds, or terrifying forests.

t: ** In what should the mind remain forbearing?

c.b: ** In what should the mind remain forbearing?
: May it show forbearance in both the loss of the desired and the encounter with the undesired.

t: ** How should all beings of the world remain?

c.b: ** How should all beings of the world remain?
: May all beings of the world remain happy, and may none of them ever be distressed.

t: ** Giving up what should we sing what?

c.b: ** Giving up what should we sing what?
: Giving up enmity, sin, and pride, may we ever sing new songs of auspiciousness.

t: ** Of what should there be talk in every home?

c.b: ** Of what should there be talk in every home?
: May there be talk of dharma (righteousness) in every home.

t: ** What is the meaning of the word "dushkrit"?

c.b: ** What is the meaning of the word "dushkrit"?
: An evil deed (sin).

t: ** By elevating what may a human birth become successful?

c.b: ** By elevating what may a human birth become successful?
: By elevating knowledge and conduct, may everyone attain the full fruit of human birth.

t: ** What should not afflict the world?

c.b: ** What should not afflict the world?
: May plague and calamity never afflict the world.

t: ** When should rain fall?

c.b: ** When should rain fall?
: May rain fall at the proper season.

t: ** How should the king be, and what should he do?

c.b: ** How should the king be, and what should he do?
: May the king, being righteous, ever administer justice to his subjects.

t: ** What should not spread in the world?

c.b: ** What should not spread in the world?
: May disease, pestilence, and famine not spread.

t: ** How should the people live?

c.b: ** How should the people live?
: May the people live in peace.

t: ** What dharma should spread in the world, and what should it do?

c.b: ** What dharma should spread in the world, and what should it do?
: May the dharma of supreme non-violence spread in the world and work for the good of all.

t: ** What should spread among people everywhere?

c.b: ** What should spread among people everywhere?
: May love spread among people everywhere, and may delusion (moha) stay far away.

t: ** What sort of words should no one speak?

c.b: ** What sort of words should no one speak?
: May no one ever speak unpleasant, bitter, or harsh words.

t: ** Reflecting on what, should one bear what with what disposition?

c.b: ** Reflecting on what, should one bear what with what disposition?
: Reflecting on the true nature of things, may everyone bear all suffering and calamity with a cheerful mind.

t: ** What is called nirvana?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** What is called nirvana?
: The complete shedding of all karmas from the soul is called nirvana.

t: ** What is called a Tirtha-kshetra?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** What is called a Tirtha-kshetra?
: A place where the auspicious events (kalyanaka) of the Tirthankaras occurred is called a Tirtha-kshetra.

t: ** What is called a Siddha-kshetra?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** What is called a Siddha-kshetra?
: A place from which any great being (mahapurush), other than a Tirthankara, attained moksha (liberation) is called a Siddha-kshetra.

t: ** What is called an Atishaya-kshetra?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** What is called an Atishaya-kshetra?
: A place where a wondrous, miraculous event occurs is called an Atishaya-kshetra.

t: ** How many verses does the Nirvana Kand contain?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** How many verses does the Nirvana Kand contain?
: The Nirvana Kand contains 20 (22) verses.

t: ** From where did Lord Adinath attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did Lord Adinath attain moksha?
: Lord Adinath attained moksha from Ashtapad (Mount Kailash).

t: ** From where did Lord Vasupujya attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did Lord Vasupujya attain moksha?
: Lord Vasupujya attained moksha from Champapur.

t: ** From where did Lord Neminath attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did Lord Neminath attain moksha?
: Lord Neminath attained moksha from Girnar.

t: ** From where did Lord Mahavir Swami attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did Lord Mahavir Swami attain moksha?
: Lord Mahavir Swami attained moksha from Pavapur.

t: ** From where did the remaining 20 Tirthankaras attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did the remaining 20 Tirthankaras attain moksha?
: Apart from Adinath, Vasupujya, Neminath, and Mahavir Swami, the remaining 20 Tirthankaras attained moksha from Sammedshikhar.

t: ** From where did 72 crore and 700 munis, along with Pradyumnakumar, attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did 72 crore and 700 munis, along with Pradyumnakumar, attain moksha?
: 72 crore and 700 munis, along with Pradyumnakumar, attained moksha from Girnarji.

t: ** From where did 5 crore munis and the sons of Ramachandra ji attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did 5 crore munis and the sons of Ramachandra ji attain moksha?
: The sons of Ramachandra ji, along with 5 crore munis, attained moksha from Pavagarh (Pavagiri).

t: ** From where did eight crore munis attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did eight crore munis attain moksha?
: 8 crore munis attained moksha from Shatrunjay and Gajpantha.

t: ** From where did the three Pandavas attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did the three Pandavas attain moksha?
: The three Pandavas attained moksha from Shatrunjay.

t: ** From where did Ram, Hanuman, and ninety-nine crore munis attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did Ram, Hanuman, and ninety-nine crore munis attain moksha?
: Ramachandra, Hanuman, and 99 crore munis attained moksha from Mangitungi.

t: ** From where did five-and-a-half crore munis attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did five-and-a-half crore munis attain moksha?
: Five-and-a-half crore munis attained moksha from Sonagiri and Revatat.

t: ** From where did Nang and Anang Kumar attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did Nang and Anang Kumar attain moksha?
: Nang and Anang Kumar attained moksha from Sonagiri.

t: ** Who attained moksha on the banks of the river Reva?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Who attained moksha on the banks of the river Reva?
: Adikumar and other munirajs, sons of Ravan, attained moksha from Revatat (the banks of the Reva).

t: ** From where did two Chakravartins and ten Kamadevas attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did two Chakravartins and ten Kamadevas attain moksha?
: Two Chakravartins and ten Kamadevas attained moksha from Siddhavarkut.

t: ** Which munirajs attained moksha from Badwani (Bawangaja)?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Which munirajs attained moksha from Badwani (Bawangaja)?
: Indrajit and Kumbhakarna attained moksha from Badwani (Bawangaja).

t: ** Which munirajs attained moksha from Pavagiri?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Which munirajs attained moksha from Pavagiri?
: Suvarnabhadra and three other munirajs attained moksha from Pavagiri.

t: ** Which Siddha-kshetra lies near the river Chelna?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Which Siddha-kshetra lies near the river Chelna?
: The Siddha-kshetra of Pavagiri lies near the river Chelna.

t: ** Which munirajs attained moksha from the Dronagiri region?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Which munirajs attained moksha from the Dronagiri region?
: Gurudatt and other munirajs attained moksha from Dronagiri.

t: ** From where did Muniraj Bali attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did Muniraj Bali attain moksha?
: Muniraj Bali attained moksha from Ashtapad.

t: ** From where did three-and-a-half crore munis attain moksha?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** From where did three-and-a-half crore munis attain moksha?
: Three-and-a-half crore munirajs attained moksha from Muktagiri and Tarangaji.

t: ** What is the other name of Medhagiri?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** What is the other name of Medhagiri?
: The other name of Medhagiri is Muktagiri.

t: ** Who attained moksha from the region of Kunthalgiri?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Who attained moksha from the region of Kunthalgiri?
: Kulabhushan and Deshabhushan Swami attained moksha from Kunthalgiri.

t: ** Who attained moksha from Nainagiri?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Who attained moksha from Nainagiri?
: Varadatta and four other munirajs attained moksha from Nainagiri.

t: ** State the special significance of Resandigiri (Nainagiri).
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** State the special significance of Resandigiri (Nainagiri).
: The samavasharan (divine assembly) of Lord Parshvanath came to Nainagiri.

t: ** State the special significance of Rajagrihi (Vipulachal).
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** State the special significance of Rajagrihi (Vipulachal).
: The samavasharan of Lord Mahavir came to Mount Vipulachal.

t: ** Who attained moksha from Mathura?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Who attained moksha from Mathura?
: Jambuswami attained moksha from Mathura.

t: ** Who composed the Nirvana Kand, and when?
grp: 8. Nirvana Kand (Canto of the Sites of Liberation)

c.b: ** Who composed the Nirvana Kand, and when?
: The Nirvana Kand was composed by Bhaiya Bhagwatidasji in the year Samvat 1741.

t: ** What is called paap (sin)?

c.b: ** What is called paap (sin)?
: That which causes the fall of the soul — bringing censure and disrepute in this life, and rebirth in hell in the next — is called paap.

t: ** How many kinds of paap are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of paap are there?
: There are five: himsa (violence), jhooth (falsehood), chori (theft), kushil (unchastity), and parigraha (possessiveness).

t: ** What is called himsa (violence)?

c.b: ** What is called himsa (violence)?
: To take life while under the sway of carelessness (pramada) is himsa.

t: ** How many kinds of himsa are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of himsa are there?
: Four kinds: sankalpi (intentional), arambhi (arising from household activity), udyogi (arising from occupation), and virodhi (arising from defensive resistance).

t: ** What is called sankalpi himsa?

c.b: ** What is called sankalpi himsa?
: Deliberately forming the intention to kill a being. In this, whether the being dies or not, sin is incurred regardless.

t: ** What is called arambhi himsa?

c.b: ** What is called arambhi himsa?
: The violence to the six classes of bodied beings (shatkaya jiva) that occurs through ordinary household activities such as drawing water, lighting fire, and cleaning the house.

t: ** What is called udyogi himsa?

c.b: ** What is called udyogi himsa?
: The violence that occurs in carrying out occupations such as farming, trade, or service/employment.

t: ** What is called virodhi himsa?

c.b: ** What is called virodhi himsa?
: The violence that occurs in resisting an attack in order to protect oneself, one's family, one's religion, or one's nation.

t: ** From which kind of himsa does a shravak (lay householder) abstain?

c.b: ** From which kind of himsa does a shravak (lay householder) abstain?
: From sankalpi himsa.

t: ** If, despite taking every precaution to protect living beings, some still die, is sin incurred?

c.b: ** If, despite taking every precaution to protect living beings, some still die, is sin incurred?
: No.

t: ** Does sin attach only to the one who kills, or to others as well?

c.b: ** Does sin attach only to the one who kills, or to others as well?
: Through commission (krita), instigation (karita), and approval (anumodana), equal sin attaches to the one who does the deed, the one who causes it to be done, and the one who approves (praises) it.

t: ** What is called jhooth (falsehood)?

c.b: ** What is called jhooth (falsehood)?
: Not to say what one has seen and heard exactly as it was, is falsehood.

t: ** If someone speaks an untruth in order to save another's life, is sin incurred?

c.b: ** If someone speaks an untruth in order to save another's life, is sin incurred?
: No sin is incurred, because in that case the intention behind the words is to save a life.

t: ** Is it true (i.e., not a fault) to call a blind man blind, or a thief a thief?

c.b: ** Is it true (i.e., not a fault) to call a blind man blind, or a thief a thief?
: To mock someone, to speak harshly, to be cruel, uncivil, or suspicious in speech, or to slander — these are sins.

t: ** How should we speak?

c.b: ** How should we speak?
: We should speak words that are beneficial, measured, and pleasant.

t: ** What is called chori (theft)?

c.b: ** What is called chori (theft)?

: To take, out of carelessness and without being given, an object that belongs to another, that has fallen, or that has been lost, without informing anyone — this is theft. As it is said: "adattadanam steyam" (taking what is not given is theft) — Tattvartha Sutra 7/15.

t: ** What is called kushil (unchastity)?

c.b: ** What is called kushil (unchastity)?
: To desire physical contact with a woman or man, out of an attachment-laden (impure) intention, is kushil.

t: (repeated as printed).** What is called parigraha (possessiveness)?

c.b: (repeated as printed).** What is called parigraha (possessiveness)?

: To feel infatuation (murchha, a craving of the mind) for a substance, whether sentient or insentient, is parigraha. As it is said: "murchha parigrahah" (attachment is possession) — Tattvartha Sutra 7/17.

t: ** What is called a vrata (vow)? How many kinds are there?

c.b: ** What is called a vrata (vow)? How many kinds are there?
: To renounce the five sins partially is an anuvrata (minor vow), and to renounce them completely is a mahavrata (great vow). There are five vows.

t: ** State the five transgressions (atichara) of the vow of ahimsa.

c.b: ** State the five transgressions (atichara) of the vow of ahimsa.
: Binding (a creature), beating it, loading it with more weight than it can bear, withholding food and water from it, and mutilating it (piercing its nose, ears, and the like).

t: ** State the five transgressions of the satya-anuvrata (vow of truthfulness).

c.b: ** State the five transgressions of the satya-anuvrata (vow of truthfulness).

: Mithyopadesh (false instruction), rahovyakhyan (disclosing others' secrets), kutalekhakriya (forgery), nyasapahar (misappropriating a trust/deposit), and sakaramantrabhed (betraying another's confidential intent through gesture).

t: ** What is called mithyopadesh?

c.b: ** What is called mithyopadesh?
: To speak against someone whose reputation is rising, contrary to the truth.

t: ** What is called rahovyakhyan?

c.b: ** What is called rahovyakhyan?
: To reveal the private conduct engaged in by a woman or man in seclusion.

t: ** What is called kutalekhakriya?

c.b: ** What is called kutalekhakriya?
: To prepare a false document in order to defraud someone.

t: ** What is called nyasapahar?

c.b: ** What is called nyasapahar?

: When someone entrusted with money, gold, or the like forgets the amount, and the depositor, mistakenly asking for less than was actually left, is told "take it, this is all you left" — that is, returning a deposit in a reduced amount, or not returning it at all.

t: ** What is called sakaramantrabhed?

c.b: ** What is called sakaramantrabhed?
: To reveal, through some pretext or other means, another's secret intention.

t: (repeated as printed).** State the five transgressions of the achaurya-vrata (vow of non-stealing).

c.b: (repeated as printed).** State the five transgressions of the achaurya-vrata (vow of non-stealing).

: Stenaprayog (encouraging theft), tadahritadan (receiving stolen goods), viruddharajyatikram (violating the state's laws), hinadhikamanonman (using false weights and measures), and pratirupakavyavahar (passing off counterfeit goods as genuine).

t: (repeated as printed).** What is called stenaprayog?

c.b: (repeated as printed).** What is called stenaprayog?
: Suggesting ways to commit theft, praising a thief, and approving of theft.

t: ** What is called tadahritadan?

c.b: ** What is called tadahritadan?
: Purchasing stolen goods.

t: ** What is viruddharajyatikram?

c.b: ** What is viruddharajyatikram?
: Acting against the laws of the state — such as buying a cheap item and selling it at an inflated price, or evading taxes.

t: ** What is called hinadhikamanonman?

c.b: ** What is called hinadhikamanonman?
: Keeping weights uneven when receiving and giving, using a scale that gives a false weight, and the like.

t: ** What is called pratirupakavyavahar?

c.b: ** What is called pratirupakavyavahar?
: Mixing a counterfeit item in with a genuine one in order to defraud others.

t: ** State the five transgressions of the brahmacharya-anuvrata (minor vow of chastity).

c.b: ** State the five transgressions of the brahmacharya-anuvrata (minor vow of chastity).

: Parvivahakaran (arranging the marriage of others), aparigrihita-itvarika-gamana (consorting with an unattached/unmarried woman), parigrihita-itvarika-gamana (consorting with another's spouse), anangakrida (unnatural sexual indulgence), and kamativrabhinivesh (intense, excessive attachment to sensual desire).

t: ** What is called parvivahakaran?

c.b: ** What is called parvivahakaran?
: Arranging engagements or marriages, without personal need, for people outside one's own household and family.

t: ** What is called aparigrihita-itvarika-gamana?

c.b: ** What is called aparigrihita-itvarika-gamana?
: Visiting prostitutes and keeping relations with them.

t: ** What is called parigrihita-itvarika-gamana?

c.b: ** What is called parigrihita-itvarika-gamana?
: Visiting and keeping contact with an unfaithful woman who, though married, has illicit relations with other men.

t: ** Why should one eat only during the day?

c.b: ** Why should one eat only during the day?
: Ultraviolet and infrared rays present in sunlight prevent the generation of minute life-forms and thus prevent the arising of disease; in this way, ahimsa (non-violence) is observed.

t: ** What does modern science say on this subject?

c.b: ** What does modern science say on this subject?
: Digestion of food occurs properly only in daylight; therefore one should eat three to four hours before sunset (bedtime).

t: ** What do other religious traditions say about eating at night?

c.b: ** What do other religious traditions say about eating at night?

: The Shantiparva of the Mahabharata states that, among the four gateways to hell, night-eating is named as the first gateway. The Markandeya Purana states that drinking water after sunset is equivalent to drinking blood, and eating grain at night is equivalent to eating flesh. The Rishishwar Bharat states that all the vows of one who consumes liquor, meat, food at night, or root vegetables (kanda-mula) come to nothing.

t: ** What harm comes from eating at night?

c.b: ** What harm comes from eating at night?

: Many kinds of illness result. If a fly is present, vomiting-inducing illness results; if even a trace of a spider [enters food], leprosy results; if a louse [enters food], dropsy results; if a hair [enters food], one's voice becomes impaired. In this way, sin of violence is incurred.

t: ** Can one eat at night by the light of a lamp?

c.b: ** Can one eat at night by the light of a lamp?

: No. Food is not digested properly [when eaten at night], causing gastric trouble, sugar (diabetes), cancer, heart attack, and the like. Nowadays the greater incidence of illness is largely due to eating at night.

t: ** What benefit comes from renouncing night-eating?

c.b: ** What benefit comes from renouncing night-eating?
: With fewer illnesses, the body stays healthy, so one's wealth is not spent on doctors; peace prevails in the home, and one is spared the sin of violence.

t: ** What is the benefit of giving up all four kinds of food at night?

c.b: ** What is the benefit of giving up all four kinds of food at night?
: It brings the merit of six months of fasting within a year, and leads to the attainment of a good rebirth.

t: ** Why should one not eat root vegetables (jamikand)?

c.b: ** Why should one not eat root vegetables (jamikand)?
: In a root vegetable such as a potato, as small as the point of a needle, there exist infinite subtle life-forms. To avoid the sin of killing those beings, one should not eat them.

t: ** What should our kitchen (bhojanshala) be like?

c.b: ** What should our kitchen (bhojanshala) be like?
: It should be like an operation theatre, where no one is allowed to enter wearing unwashed clothes.

t: ** How should one eat one's food?

c.b: ** How should one eat one's food?
: One should not watch television or the like while eating, and one should eat in silence.

t: ** What harm comes from eating while watching television?

c.b: ** What harm comes from eating while watching television?
: At that time, one's attention is fixed not on the food but on the television, so that one does not even notice what one is eating.

t: ** What is called janma (birth)?

c.b: ** What is called janma (birth)?
: The obtaining of a new body upon leaving the previous body is called janma.

t: ** How many kinds of janma are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of janma are there?
: Three kinds: sammurchhan (spontaneous generation), garbhaja (birth from a womb), and upapada (instantaneous birth).

t: ** What is called sammurchhan janma?

c.b: ** What is called sammurchhan janma?
: The formation of a body — without needing the union of the father's and mother's reproductive fluids (raja-virya) — from material particles (pudgala paramanu) suited for it, is sammurchhan janma.

t: ** What is called garbha janma (birth from a womb)?

c.b: ** What is called garbha janma (birth from a womb)?
: The formation of a body in the mother's womb through the union of the father's and mother's reproductive fluids.

t: ** What is called upapada janma?

c.b: ** What is called upapada janma?
: The formation of a body, without the union of the parents' reproductive fluids, from material particles at a fixed location (such as an "upapada-shayya," a birth-couch).

t: ** To whom does sammurchhan janma belong?

c.b: ** To whom does sammurchhan janma belong?

: All beings from one-sensed up through four-sensed beings are invariably sammurchhan-born. Some five-sensed animals (tiryancha) and undeveloped (aparyapta) human beings can also have sammurchhan birth.

t: ** How many kinds of garbha janma (womb-birth) are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of garbha janma (womb-birth) are there?
: Three kinds: jarayuja, andaja, and potaja.

t: ** What is called jarayuja?

c.b: ** What is called jarayuja?
: A being born wrapped in a sac-like membrane resembling flesh and blood, similar to filth (mala).

t: ** What is called andaja?

c.b: ** What is called andaja?
: A being that is born from an egg.

t: ** What is called potaja?

c.b: ** What is called potaja?
: Beings that, at the moment of birth, are already free from any such enveloping membrane, and are able to move about immediately.

t: ** To whom does upapada janma belong?

c.b: ** To whom does upapada janma belong?
: To celestial beings (deva) and to hell-beings (naraki).

t: ** What is called avagahana?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is called avagahana?
: The height of the body (utsedha) is called avagahana.

t: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a one-sensed being?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a one-sensed being?
: A little over one thousand yojanas — as in the case of a lotus and the like.

t: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a two-sensed being?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a two-sensed being?
: Twelve yojanas — as in the case of a conch and the like.

t: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a three-sensed being?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a three-sensed being?
: Three kos — as in the case of an ant and the like.

t: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a four-sensed being?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a four-sensed being?
: One yojana — as in the case of a bee and the like.

t: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a five-sensed being?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a five-sensed being?
: One thousand yojanas — as in the case of the mahamatsya (the great fish) and the like.

t: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a human being, and where is it found?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a human being, and where is it found?
: Three kos, in the finest bhogabhumi (land of enjoyment).

t: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a human being in the karmabhumi (land of action)?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is the maximum avagahana of a human being in the karmabhumi (land of action)?
: 525 dhanusha (bow-lengths), as in the case of Bahubali.

t: ** What is the measure of a yojana and of a dhanusha (bow-length)?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What is the measure of a yojana and of a dhanusha (bow-length)?
: A yojana equals eight miles, and a dhanusha (bow-length) equals four hastas (hand-lengths/cubits).

t: ** What are the minimum and maximum avagahana of hell-beings?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What are the minimum and maximum avagahana of hell-beings?
: In the first hell, the minimum avagahana is three hastas, and in the seventh hell, the maximum avagahana is five hundred dhanusha.

t: ** What are the minimum and maximum avagahana of celestial beings?
grp: 11. Avagahana (Bodily Height / Space-Points Occupied by the Soul)

c.b: ** What are the minimum and maximum avagahana of celestial beings?
: The minimum avagahana of the gods of Sarvarthasiddhi is one hasta, and the maximum avagahana of the Asurakumar gods is twenty-five dhanusha.

t: ** What is called yoni?

c.b: ** What is called yoni?
: The basis/site of birth is called yoni.

t: ** How many kinds of yoni are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of yoni are there?
: There are two principal kinds: akara-yoni and guna-yoni.

t: ** How many kinds of akara-yoni are there? Name and describe them.

c.b: ** How many kinds of akara-yoni are there? Name and describe them.

: Three kinds: shankhavarta, kurmonnata, and vamshapatra. (1) In the shankhavarta yoni, no embryo takes hold. (2) In the kurmonnata yoni, great beings such as the Tirthankaras take birth. (3) In the vamshapatra yoni, ordinary men and women take birth.

t: ** Name and describe the kinds of guna-yoni.

c.b: ** Name and describe the kinds of guna-yoni.

: There are nine kinds: sachitta (associated with living matter), shita (cold), samvrita (concealed), achitta (associated with non-living matter), ushna (hot), vivrita (open/exposed), sachittachitta (mixed living/non-living), shitoshna (mixed cold/hot), and samvritavivrita (mixed concealed/exposed).

t: ** What is called samvrita-yoni?

c.b: ** What is called samvrita-yoni?
: A yoni that is not visible, being covered/enclosed, is called samvrita-yoni.

t: ** What is called shita-yoni?

c.b: ** What is called shita-yoni?
: A yoni possessed of a cold touch is called shita-yoni.

t: ** What is called sachitta-yoni?

c.b: ** What is called sachitta-yoni?
: A yoni that possesses life (associated with a living substance) is called sachitta-yoni.
