t: ** How many divisions does guna-yoni have by extent, and of what sort?

c.b: ** How many divisions does guna-yoni have by extent, and of what sort?

: By extent, there are 8,400,000 (84 lakh) divisions: one-sensed beings — 52 lakh; two-sensed beings — 2 lakh; three-sensed beings — 2 lakh; four-sensed beings — 2 lakh; five-sensed animals (tiryancha) — 4 lakh; gods — 4 lakh; hell-beings — 4 lakh; and humans — 14 lakh.

t: ** How do the 52 lakh yonis of one-sensed beings arise?

c.b: ** How do the 52 lakh yonis of one-sensed beings arise?

: [They consist of:] the earth-bodied, water-bodied, fire-bodied, and air-bodied beings — each of the general (itara-nigoda) and permanent (nitya-nigoda) categories — 7 lakh each (7×6 = 42 lakh), plus the plant-bodied (vanaspatikaya) beings — 10 lakh. In this way, 42 lakh plus 10 lakh together make 52 lakh divisions.

t: ** What is called jiva samasa?

c.b: ** What is called jiva samasa?
: That by which many souls are grouped together (into classes) is called jiva samasa.

t: ** How many divisions does jiva samasa have?

c.b: ** How many divisions does jiva samasa have?
: Jiva samasa has fourteen divisions.

t: ** Are all souls both sukshma (subtle/microscopic) and badar (gross)?

c.b: ** Are all souls both sukshma (subtle/microscopic) and badar (gross)?
: No — only one-sensed beings have both the sukshma and badar divisions. Beings with mobility (trasa) are invariably badar (gross).

t: ** What are called a badar jiva (gross soul) and a badar body?

c.b: ** What are called a badar jiva (gross soul) and a badar body?
: Through the rise of badar-nama-karma, a soul is called badar. A body that obstructs another, or is itself obstructed by another, is called a badar (gross) body.

t: ** What are called a sukshma jiva (subtle soul) and a sukshma body?

c.b: ** What are called a sukshma jiva (subtle soul) and a sukshma body?
: Through the rise of sukshma-nama-karma, a soul is called sukshma. A body that neither obstructs another nor is itself obstructed by another is called a sukshma (subtle) body.

t: ** State the sub-divisions (uttarabheda) of jiva samasa.

c.b: ** State the sub-divisions (uttarabheda) of jiva samasa.
: The sub-divisions of jiva samasa number ninety-eight (98).

t: ** Among whom are these ninety-eight sub-divisions of jiva samasa distributed?

c.b: ** Among whom are these ninety-eight sub-divisions of jiva samasa distributed?
: Among the tiryancha (animals) — 85; among humans — 9; among hell-beings (naraki) — 2; and among celestial beings (deva) — 2 — making 98 sub-types in total.

t: ** What are the 85 sub-types of tiryancha (animal/plant beings)?

c.b: ** What are the 85 sub-types of tiryancha (animal/plant beings)?
: The sammurcchana (spontaneously-born, non-sexually generated) tiryanchas have 69 sub-types and the garbhaja (womb-born) tiryanchas have 16; together these make 85 sub-types of tiryancha.

t: ** What are the 69 jiva-samasa (soul-classes) of sammurcchana tiryancha?

c.b: ** What are the 69 jiva-samasa (soul-classes) of sammurcchana tiryancha?
: Ekendriya (one-sensed beings) have 42, vikalatraya (the two-, three- and four-sensed beings) have 9, and sammurcchana panchendriya (five-sensed) tiryanchas have 18 — together making 69.

t: ** What are the 42 sub-types of ekendriya?

c.b: ** What are the 42 sub-types of ekendriya?

: Earth-bodied, water-bodied, fire-bodied, air-bodied, nitya-nigoda and itara-nigoda beings — these six, considered as bādara (gross) and sūkṣma (subtle), give 12 types. Adding sapratiṣṭhita (with a co-resident basis) and apratiṣṭhita (without one) vegetable-bodied beings makes 14. Multiplying these 14 by paryāptaka (fully developed), nivṛtti-paryāptaka (formation-complete) and labdhi-aparyāptaka (potentially undeveloped) gives 42 sub-types.

t: ** What are the 9 sub-types of vikalatraya?

c.b: ** What are the 9 sub-types of vikalatraya?
: Two-sensed, three-sensed and four-sensed beings, each multiplied by paryāptaka, nivṛtti-paryāptaka and labdhi-aparyāptaka, give the 9 sub-types of vikalatraya.

t: ** What are the 18 sub-types of sammurcchana panchendriya?

c.b: ** What are the 18 sub-types of sammurcchana panchendriya?

: Water-dwellers, land-dwellers and sky-dwellers, each considered as saṁjñī (rational/possessing a mind) and asaṁjñī (non-rational), give 6 types. Multiplying these 6 by paryāptaka, nivṛtti-paryāptaka and labdhi-aparyāptaka gives 18 sub-types.

t: ** What are the 16 sub-types of garbhaja (womb-born) panchendriya?

c.b: ** What are the 16 sub-types of garbhaja (womb-born) panchendriya?
: Karmabhūmi (land-of-action) beings have 12 and bhogabhūmi (land-of-enjoyment) beings have 4; together these make the 16 sub-types of garbhaja panchendriya.

t: ** What are the 12 sub-types of karmabhūmi (beings)?

c.b: ** What are the 12 sub-types of karmabhūmi (beings)?
: Water-dwellers, land-dwellers and sky-dwellers, considered as saṁjñī and asaṁjñī, give 6 types. Considering these as paryāptaka and nivṛtti-paryāptaka gives 12 sub-types.

t: ** What are the four sub-types of bhogabhūmi (beings)?

c.b: ** What are the four sub-types of bhogabhūmi (beings)?
: Land-dwellers and sky-dwellers, considered as paryāptaka and nivṛtti-paryāptaka, give four sub-types. In bhogabhūmi there are no water-dwelling or asaṁjñī tiryanchas.

t: ** What are the nine sub-types of humans?

c.b: ** What are the nine sub-types of humans?

: Ārya-khaṇḍa, Mleccha-khaṇḍa, bhogabhūmi and kubhogabhūmi (inferior land-of-enjoyment) humans — these four types of garbhaja (womb-born) humans, considered as paryāptaka and nivṛtti-paryāptaka, give 8 types. Adding the sammurcchana (spontaneously-born) human labdhi-aparyāptaka type makes nine.

t: ** What are the two sub-types of hell-beings (naraki)?

c.b: ** What are the two sub-types of hell-beings (naraki)?
: Paryāptaka and nivṛtti-paryāptaka.

t: ** What are the two sub-types of devas?

c.b: ** What are the two sub-types of devas?
: Paryāptaka and nivṛtti-paryāptaka.

t: ** How are the 19 jiva-samasas (classes of souls) arrived at?

c.b: ** How are the 19 jiva-samasas (classes of souls) arrived at?

: Earth-bodied, water-bodied, fire-bodied, air-bodied, itara-nigoda and nitya-nigoda beings — these six, considered as sūkṣma (subtle) and bādara (gross), give 12 types. Adding two types of vegetable-bodied beings — sapratiṣṭhita pratyeka and apratiṣṭhita pratyeka — gives 14 types of sthāvara (immobile beings) in all. Adding the three vikalatraya classes and the saṁjñī and asaṁjñī panchendriya classes brings the total to 19.

t: ** How are the 57 jiva-samasas arrived at?

c.b: ** How are the 57 jiva-samasas arrived at?
: Considering each of the above 19 types as paryāpta, aparyāpta and labdhi-aparyāpta gives 57 sub-types.

t: ** What is margana (soul-quest)? How many are there?

c.b: ** What is margana (soul-quest)? How many are there?
: The investigation (search) of souls in their various modes of existence, by means of their psychic dispositions (bhava), is called margana. There are fourteen of these.

t: ** Name the marganas.

c.b: ** Name the marganas.

: Gati (destiny), indriya (sense), kaya (body-class), yoga (activity), veda (sex-disposition), kashaya (passion), jnana (knowledge), samyam (self-restraint), darshan (perception), leshya (thought-colouration), bhavyatva (fitness for liberation), samyaktva (right faith), samjni (rationality) and aharaka (nutrition-intake).

t: ** What is gati? How many are there? Name them.

c.b: ** What is gati? How many are there? Name them.

: The particular state of a soul attained through the rise of jāti-nāmakarma (destiny-determining karma) is called gati. There are four: naraka-gati (hell), tiryancha-gati (animal/plant), manushya-gati (human), deva-gati (celestial).

t: ** What is indriya (sense organ)? How many are there? Name them.

c.b: ** What is indriya (sense organ)? How many are there? Name them.

: The particular external mark of a worldly soul, arising through the kṣayopaśama (destruction-cum-subsidence) of indriyāvaraṇa karma (sense-obscuring karma), is called an indriya. There are five: touch (sparshana), taste (rasana), smell (ghrana), sight (chakshu), and hearing (karna).

t: ** How many kinds of indriya are there? Name them.

c.b: ** How many kinds of indriya are there? Name them.
: There are two kinds of indriya — (1) dravya-indriya (physical sense organ) and (2) bhava-indriya (psychic sense organ).

t: ** What is dravya-indriya?

c.b: ** What is dravya-indriya?
: Nivritti (the physical formation) and upakarana (the auxiliary structure) together are called dravya-indriya.

t: ** What is bhava-indriya?

c.b: ** What is bhava-indriya?
: Labdhi (the capacity/attainment) and upayoga (the cognitive application) together are called bhava-indriya.

t: ** What is nivritti? How many kinds are there?

c.b: ** What is nivritti? How many kinds are there?

: The particular configuration of the soul's space-points [that forms a sense organ] is called nivritti. It is of two kinds: bāhya-nivritti (external formation) and abhyantara-nivritti (internal formation).

t: ** What is bāhya-nivritti (external formation)?

c.b: ** What is bāhya-nivritti (external formation)?
: The particular configuration of pudgala (matter) in the shape of a sense organ is called bāhya-nivritti.

t: ** What is abhyantara-nivritti (internal formation)?

c.b: ** What is abhyantara-nivritti (internal formation)?
: The particular configuration, in the shape of a sense organ, of the soul's own purified space-points is called abhyantara-nivritti.

t: ** What is upakarana (the auxiliary organ)? How many kinds are there? Name them.

c.b: ** What is upakarana (the auxiliary organ)? How many kinds are there? Name them.
: That which protects/assists the nivritti is upakarana. It is of two kinds — (1) bāhya (external) (2) abhyantara (internal).

t: ** What is bāhya (external) upakarana?

c.b: ** What is bāhya (external) upakarana?
: That which assists the nivritti the way the eyelid assists the organ of sight.

t: ** What is abhyantara (internal) upakarana?

c.b: ** What is abhyantara (internal) upakarana?
: That which assists the nivritti in every sense organ the way the black and white portions [of the pupil] assist the organ of sight.

t: ** What is labdhi?

c.b: ** What is labdhi?
: The kṣayopaśama (destruction-cum-subsidence) of jñānāvaraṇa karma (knowledge-obscuring karma) is called labdhi.

t: ** What is upayoga?

c.b: ** What is upayoga?
: The particular modification of consciousness that results from that kṣayopaśama is called upayoga.

t: ** What is kaya (body-class)?

c.b: ** What is kaya (body-class)?

: The mode of existence arising through the rise of trasa-nāmakarma and sthāvara-nāmakarma (mobile-being and immobile-being determining karma) is called kaya. The mass of matter accumulated through yoga (activity) is called kaya-margana.

t: ** How many kinds of kaya are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of kaya are there?
: There are six kinds of kaya: earth, water, fire, air, vegetation, and trasa (mobile beings) — that is, the five sthāvara (immobile) classes and one trasa class.

t: ** What is yoga? How many kinds are there?

c.b: ** What is yoga? How many kinds are there?

: The power, arising through the rise of body-determining karma, that causes a soul possessed of mind, speech and body to draw in karmas, is called yoga. There are three: mind (mana), speech (vachana), body (kaya).

t: ** How many sub-types does yoga-margana have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many sub-types does yoga-margana have? Name them.

: Yoga-margana has 15 sub-types. Mano-yoga (mental activity) and vachana-yoga (vocal activity) each have 4 (true, untrue, mixed, neither-true-nor-untrue), and kaya-yoga (bodily activity) has 7 — audarika (physical), audarika-mishra (physical-mixed), vaikriyika (transformable), vaikriyika-mishra (transformable-mixed), aharaka (projectable), aharaka-mishra (projectable-mixed) and karmana (karmic).

t: ** What is veda (sex-disposition)?

c.b: ** What is veda (sex-disposition)?

: The desire for sexual union that arises in a soul through the rise of the no-kashaya called veda is called bhava-veda (psychic gender). The particular bodily mark manifested through nama-karma is called dravya-veda (physical gender).

t: ** How many kinds of veda are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of veda are there?
: Stri-veda (female), purusha-veda (male), napumsaka-veda (neuter).

t: ** What is kashaya (passion)?

c.b: ** What is kashaya (passion)?
: That which harms the soul's states of samyaktva (right faith), partial conduct, complete conduct and yathakhyata (ideal) conduct is called kashaya.

t: ** How many kinds of kashaya are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of kashaya are there?

: There are twenty-five: anantanubandhi (endless-binding — anger, pride, deceit, greed), apratyakhyana (partial-vow-obstructing — anger, pride, deceit, greed), pratyakhyana (full-vow-obstructing — anger, pride, deceit, greed), sanjvalana (subtle-conduct-obstructing — anger, pride, deceit, greed), plus laughter, liking, disliking, sorrow, fear, disgust, female-gender, male-gender and neuter-gender. [This makes] 16 kashayas and 9 no-kashayas.

t: ** What is jnana (knowledge)?

c.b: ** What is jnana (knowledge)?
: That quality of the soul by which it knows objects pertaining to the three times [past, present, future] is called jnana (the knowledge-quality).

t: ** How many kinds of jnana-margana are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of jnana-margana are there?

: Jnana-margana has eight kinds: mati-jnana (sensory/rational knowledge), shruta-jnana (scriptural knowledge), avadhi-jnana (clairvoyance), manahparyaya-jnana (mind-reading knowledge), kevala-jnana (omniscience), ku-mati-jnana, ku-shruta-jnana and ku-avadhi-jnana (their respective false/perverted counterparts).

t: ** How many are the valid means of knowledge (pramana-jnana)?

c.b: ** How many are the valid means of knowledge (pramana-jnana)?
: Mati, shruta, avadhi, manahparyaya and kevala-jnana — these constitute right knowledge (samyag-jnana), which is pramana (a valid means of knowledge).

t: ** How many limbs (anga) does samyag-jnana (right knowledge) have? What are they?

c.b: ** How many limbs (anga) does samyag-jnana (right knowledge) have? What are they?

: Samyag-jnana has eight limbs: 1. vyanjana-vyanjitaya, 2. artha-samagraya, 3. tadubhaya-samagraya, 4. kaladhyayanaya, 5. upadhyanopahitaya, 6. vinaya-labdhi-prabhavanaya, 7. guru-vadahvaya, 8. bahumanonmanaya.

t: ** What is vyanjana-vyanjitaya?

c.b: ** What is vyanjana-vyanjitaya?
: Reading the letters and consonants correctly.

t: ** What is artha-samagraya?

c.b: ** What is artha-samagraya?
: Pronouncing correctly along with the meaning.

t: ** What is tadubhaya-samagraya?

c.b: ** What is tadubhaya-samagraya?
: Reading the letters and consonants together with the meaning.

t: ** What is kaladhyayanaya?

c.b: ** What is kaladhyayanaya?
: Studying scripture only during its prescribed time, and not studying it at an improper time.

t: ** What is upadhyanopahitaya?

c.b: ** What is upadhyanopahitaya?
: Not abandoning a scriptural text one has begun studying until it is completed.

t: ** What is vinaya-labdhi-prabhavanaya?

c.b: ** What is vinaya-labdhi-prabhavanaya?
: Showing reverence to the Jina's teaching (Jinavani), and studying with due reverence.

t: ** What is guru-vadahvaya?

c.b: ** What is guru-vadahvaya?
: Not concealing the name of the teacher from whom one learned.

t: ** What is bahumanonmanaya?

c.b: ** What is bahumanonmanaya?
: Showing great reverence toward one's teacher.

t: ** What is samyam (self-restraint)?

c.b: ** What is samyam (self-restraint)?
: Taking vows, observing the samitis (rules of careful conduct), restraining the passions, renouncing sensual enjoyments, and conquering the senses — this is called samyam.

t: ** How many kinds of samyam-margana are there? Name them.

c.b: ** How many kinds of samyam-margana are there? Name them.
: Samyam-margana has 7 kinds: samayika, chhedopasthapana, parihara-vishuddhi, sukshma-samparaya, yathakhyata, samyamasamyam, and asamyam.

t: ** What is darshan (perception)?

c.b: ** What is darshan (perception)?

: Grasping only the general aspect — not the particular aspect — of an object that has both general and particular characteristics is called darshan. It is of 4 kinds — (1) chakshu-darshan (visual perception) (2) achakshu-darshan (non-visual perception) (3) avadhi-darshan (clairvoyant perception) (4) kevala-darshan (perfect perception).

t: ** What is leshya (thought-colouration)? How many kinds are there?

c.b: ** What is leshya (thought-colouration)? How many kinds are there?
: The activity of yoga as coloured by kashaya (passion) is called leshya. It has six kinds: 1. krishna (black) 2. nila (blue) 3. kapota (grey) 4. peeta (yellow) 5. padma (pink) 6. shukla (white).

t: ** What is bhavya-margana? How many kinds are there?

c.b: ** What is bhavya-margana? How many kinds are there?

: It is the investigation of whether a worldly soul has the inherent fitness (bhavyatva) to attain liberation or not. It has two kinds: 1. bhavyatva (fit for liberation) 2. abhavyatva (never fit for liberation).

t: ** What is samyaktva-margana? How many kinds does it have?

c.b: ** What is samyaktva-margana? How many kinds does it have?

: Firm faith in the seven tattvas (fundamental realities) as taught by the Jina is called samyaktva. It has six kinds: 1. upashama (subsidential) 2. kshayopashamika (destructive-cum-subsidential) 3. kshayika (purely destructive) 4. mithyatva (wrong faith) 5. sasadana (faith on the verge of falling) 6. mishra (mixed).

t: ** What is upashama-samyaktva?

c.b: ** What is upashama-samyaktva?
: The samyaktva that arises from the subsidence of the four anantanubandhi kashayas together with mithyatva, samyagmithyatva and samyak-prakriti — these seven karmic natures.

t: ** What is kshayopashamika (vedaka) samyaktva?

c.b: ** What is kshayopashamika (vedaka) samyaktva?

: The samyaktva that arises from the operative-destruction (udayabhavi-kshaya) of the four anantanubandhi kashayas together with mithyatva and samyagmithyatva — these six natures — combined with their subsidence-in-potential-existence and the rise of the samyaktva-prakriti.

t: ** What is kshayika samyaktva?

c.b: ** What is kshayika samyaktva?
: The samyaktva that arises from the complete destruction of the four anantanubandhi kashayas together with the three natures of darshana-mohaniya (faith-deluding karma) — these seven natures.

t: ** What is samjni (rational)? How many kinds are there?

c.b: ** What is samjni (rational)? How many kinds are there?

: The knowledge produced by the kshayopashama of no-indriyavarana karma (mind-obscuring karma) is called samjna (mind). One who possesses this samjna (mind) is called samjni, and one who lacks mind is called asamjni.

t: ** What is ahara-margana (nutrition-quest)? How many kinds are there?

c.b: ** What is ahara-margana (nutrition-quest)? How many kinds are there?

: The taking-in of the matter-particles (ahara-vargana) suitable for forming the body and completing the paryaptis (developmental capacities) is called ahara-margana. It has two kinds: 1. aharaka (nutrition-taking) 2. anaharaka (non-nutrition-taking).

t: ** How many are the sub-types (uttara-bheda) of the fourteen marganas?

c.b: ** How many are the sub-types (uttara-bheda) of the fourteen marganas?
: There are 95 sub-types.

t: ** What is dravya (substance)?

c.b: ** What is dravya (substance)?

: The aggregate of qualities (gunas) is called dravya. Origination, cessation and permanence (utpada, vyaya, dhrauvya) together constitute dravya. That which possesses qualities (guna) and modes (paryaya) is called dravya.

t: ** How many dravyas are there?

c.b: ** How many dravyas are there?
: There are six dravyas: 1. jiva (soul), 2. pudgala (matter), 3. dharma (medium of motion), 4. adharma (medium of rest), 5. akasha (space) and 6. kala (time).

t: ** How many dravyas are murtika (corporeal)?

c.b: ** How many dravyas are murtika (corporeal)?
: Only one dravya, pudgala, is corporeal.

t: ** How many dravyas have asankhyata (innumerable) space-points?

c.b: ** How many dravyas have asankhyata (innumerable) space-points?
: Four dravyas — jiva, pudgala, dharma, adharma.

t: ** How many dravyas are parinami (subject to modification) and sakriya (active/in motion)? Name them.

c.b: ** How many dravyas are parinami (subject to modification) and sakriya (active/in motion)? Name them.
: Two dravyas — jiva and pudgala.

t: ** Which dravyas are, in a certain sense, single (only one of their kind)?

c.b: ** Which dravyas are, in a certain sense, single (only one of their kind)?
: Dharma, adharma, akasha.

t: ** In what respect is jiva dravya said to be corporeal?

c.b: ** In what respect is jiva dravya said to be corporeal?
: In respect of its association with karmas, jiva dravya is called corporeal.

t: ** Define jiva dravya.

c.b: ** Define jiva dravya.
: That in which the characteristic of knowledge-and-perception-consciousness is found.

t: ** What is pudgala dravya?

c.b: ** What is pudgala dravya?
: That in which touch, taste, smell and colour are found.

t: ** How many kinds of pudgala dravya are there? Name them.

c.b: ** How many kinds of pudgala dravya are there? Name them.
: Paramanu (atom) and skandha (aggregate/molecule).

t: ** What is a paramanu (atom)?

c.b: ** What is a paramanu (atom)?
: The smallest part of pudgala — one that cannot be further divided or broken — is called a paramanu. It occupies a single space-point.

t: ** What is a skandha (aggregate)?

c.b: ** What is a skandha (aggregate)?
: A collection of two or more paramanus is called a skandha. Skandhas may occupy a numerable, innumerable or even infinite number of space-points.

t: ** What is dharma dravya?

c.b: ** What is dharma dravya?
: That which, while itself motionless, assists jiva and pudgala in moving.

t: ** What is adharma dravya?

c.b: ** What is adharma dravya?
: That which, while itself motionless, assists jiva and pudgala in coming to rest.

t: ** What is akasha (space) dravya?

c.b: ** What is akasha (space) dravya?
: That which provides room for all substances to exist in.

t: ** How many kinds of akasha are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of akasha are there?
: There are two kinds: loka-akasha (the space occupied by the universe) and aloka-akasha (space beyond it).

t: ** What is loka-akasha?

c.b: ** What is loka-akasha?
: That space in which all six dravyas exist is called loka-akasha. It has three parts: adho-loka (lower world), madhya-loka (middle world), urdhva-loka (upper world).

t: ** What is aloka-akasha?

c.b: ** What is aloka-akasha?
: The space lying beyond loka-akasha is called aloka-akasha.

t: ** What is kala (time) dravya?

c.b: ** What is kala (time) dravya?

: That which assists all substances in their modification (parinamana) is called kala. It has two aspects — nishchaya-kala (real/absolute time) and vyavahara-kala (conventional time). The kalanu (atom of time) is called nishchaya-kala, while units such as the ghadi, ghanta (hour), day and night are called vyavahara-kala.

t: ** What is the distinguishing quality of each of the six dravyas?

c.b: ** What is the distinguishing quality of each of the six dravyas?

: Jiva dravya — the characteristic of consciousness. Pudgala dravya — touch, taste, smell, colour. Dharma dravya — the property of being an aid to motion. Adharma dravya — the property of being an aid to rest. Akasha dravya — the property of providing space (avagahana). Kala dravya — the property of being an aid to modification (parinamana).

t: ** What are the general (samanya) qualities common to all dravyas? Name them.

c.b: ** What are the general (samanya) qualities common to all dravyas? Name them.

: Existence (astitva), thing-hood (vastutva), substance-hood (dravyatva), knowability (prameyatva), non-heaviness/non-lightness (agurulaghutva), space-point-hood (pradeshatva), non-consciousness (achetanatva) and formlessness (amurtatva), etc.

t: ** What is tattva? How many kinds are there? Name them.

c.b: ** What is tattva? How many kinds are there? Name them.

: The true nature of a thing is called tattva. There are seven: jiva (soul), ajiva (non-soul), asrava (influx of karma), bandha (bondage), samvara (stoppage of influx), nirjara (partial shedding of karma) and moksha (liberation).

t: ** What is jiva-tattva?

c.b: ** What is jiva-tattva?
: That in which knowledge and perception (consciousness) are found is called jiva.

t: ** What is ajiva-tattva?

c.b: ** What is ajiva-tattva?
: That in which knowledge and perception (consciousness) are not found is called ajiva.

t: ** What is asrava-tattva?

c.b: ** What is asrava-tattva?
: The inflow of karmas [into the soul] is called asrava. It has two kinds — dravya-asrava, bhava-asrava.

t: ** What is dravya-asrava?

c.b: ** What is dravya-asrava?
: The transformation of karmic matter-particles (karmana varganas) into the form of karma, as they come in, is called dravya-asrava.

t: ** What is bhava-asrava?

c.b: ** What is bhava-asrava?
: The soul's disposition of attachment and aversion (raga-dvesha) is called bhava-asrava.

t: ** What is bandha-tattva (bondage)? How many kinds does it have? Name them.

c.b: ** What is bandha-tattva (bondage)? How many kinds does it have? Name them.
: The soul's space-points and the karmic space-points occupying the same location is called bandha-tattva. It has two kinds — dravya-bandha, bhava-bandha.

t: ** Define dravya-bandha and bhava-bandha.

c.b: ** Define dravya-bandha and bhava-bandha.
: The occupying of the same space by karmana varganas and the soul is dravya-bandha, while the psychic states owing to which this bondage occurs are called bhava-bandha.

t: ** What is samvara-tattva?

c.b: ** What is samvara-tattva?
: The stopping of asrava is samvara. It has two kinds — dravya-samvara, bhava-samvara.

t: ** What are dravya-samvara and bhava-samvara?

c.b: ** What are dravya-samvara and bhava-samvara?

: The non-arrival of karmana varganas is dravya-samvara, while the psychic states owing to which the disposition of attachment-aversion is halted and the inflow of karmana varganas stops are called bhava-samvara.

t: ** What is nirjara-tattva?

c.b: ** What is nirjara-tattva?
: The partial shedding of karmas from the soul is called nirjara. It has two kinds — dravya-nirjara, bhava-nirjara.

t: ** What is moksha-tattva?

c.b: ** What is moksha-tattva?
: The complete separation of dravya-karma, bhava-karma and no-karma (quasi-karmic matter) from the soul is called moksha. It has two kinds — dravya-moksha and bhava-moksha.

t: ** Define dravya-moksha and bhava-moksha.

c.b: ** Define dravya-moksha and bhava-moksha.
: The complete destruction of dravya-karmas [from the soul] is dravya-moksha, and the psychic states by which all the soul's karmas are destroyed is called bhava-moksha.

t: ** Which are the upadeya (worth-adopting) tattvas?

c.b: ** Which are the upadeya (worth-adopting) tattvas?
: Jiva, samvara, nirjara and moksha.

t: ** Which are the heya (worth-rejecting) tattvas?

c.b: ** Which are the heya (worth-rejecting) tattvas?
: Ajiva, asrava and bandha.

t: ** List the categories of padartha (the fundamental entities) by name.

c.b: ** List the categories of padartha (the fundamental entities) by name.
: Jiva, ajiva, asrava, bandha, samvara, nirjara, moksha, punya (merit) and papa (demerit/sin).

t: ** What is punya (merit)?

c.b: ** What is punya (merit)?
: That which purifies the soul is called punya.

t: ** What is papa (sin)?

c.b: ** What is papa (sin)?
: That which defiles (degrades) the soul is called papa.

t: ** Within which tattva are punya and papa included?

c.b: ** Within which tattva are punya and papa included?
: Within the asrava tattva.

t: ** What are the causes of asrava?

c.b: ** What are the causes of asrava?
: Mithyatva (wrong faith), avirati (lack of restraint), pramada (carelessness), kashaya (passion), and yoga (activity).

t: ** How many kinds of mithyatva are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of mithyatva are there?
: Five kinds — viparita (perverse), ekanta (one-sided), vinaya (excessive-deference), samshaya (doubting), and ajnana (ignorance-based).

t: ** What is avirati?

c.b: ** What is avirati?
: Not showing compassion toward the beings of the six kayas (the six classes of living bodies), and not bringing the five senses and the mind under control — this is avirati.

t: ** What is pramada? How many kinds does it have?

c.b: ** What is pramada? How many kinds does it have?
: Disregard for virtuous activity is pramada. It has 15 kinds: 4 vikathas (idle/harmful talk), 4 kashayas, 5 sense-objects, sleep, and attachment (sneha).

t: ** How many sub-types (uttara-bheda) does asrava have?

c.b: ** How many sub-types (uttara-bheda) does asrava have?
: 57. Five [types of] mithyatva, 12 avirati, 25 kashaya, 15 yoga.

t: ** Why has pramada not been included here [in this count]?

c.b: ** Why has pramada not been included here [in this count]?
: Pramada has already been subsumed within kashaya.

t: ** What is dhyana (meditation)?

c.b: ** What is dhyana (meditation)?

: Concentrating the mind single-pointedly on one object is dhyana. It has four kinds: arta-dhyana (sorrowful meditation), raudra-dhyana (cruel meditation), dharma-dhyana (righteous meditation), shukla-dhyana (pure meditation).

t: ** Which meditations are causes of samsara (worldly bondage), and which are causes of moksha?

c.b: ** Which meditations are causes of samsara (worldly bondage), and which are causes of moksha?
: Arta-dhyana and raudra-dhyana are causes of samsara, while dharma-dhyana and shukla-dhyana are causes of moksha.

t: ** Who can meditate, and for how long can meditation continue at most?

c.b: ** Who can meditate, and for how long can meditation continue at most?
: Only those possessed of an excellent samhanana (skeletal constitution) can meditate, and even then only for an antarmuhurta (a fraction of a muhurta) at most.

t: ** What are the excellent samhananas?

c.b: ** What are the excellent samhananas?
: Vajra-vrishabha-naracha, vajra-naracha, and naracha-samhanana.

t: ** What is an antarmuhurta?

c.b: ** What is an antarmuhurta?
: A period of forty-eight minutes is called a muhurta; the time between an avali and a full muhurta is called an antarmuhurta.

t: ** What are samaya (instant) and avali?

c.b: ** What are samaya (instant) and avali?
: The smallest mode/unit of kala-dravya (time) is called a samaya. An innumerable number of samayas make one avali.

t: ** How many kinds of arta-dhyana are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of arta-dhyana are there?
: Four: ishta-viyoga (separation from what is liked), anishta-samyoga (union with what is disliked), pida-chintana (brooding over pain), nidana-bandha (longing for future pleasures).

t: ** What is ishta-viyoga arta-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is ishta-viyoga arta-dhyana?
: The brooding that occurs, seeking reunion, when one is separated from a beloved object.

t: ** What is anishta-samyoga arta-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is anishta-samyoga arta-dhyana?
: The brooding done to find release when one is united with an undesired object.

t: ** What is pida-chintana arta-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is pida-chintana arta-dhyana?
: Brooding, whenever any kind of pain occurs, over when it will end.

t: ** What is nidana-bandha arta-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is nidana-bandha arta-dhyana?
: Brooding with the aim of obtaining worldly pleasures in the future.

t: ** What is raudra-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is raudra-dhyana?

: Taking delight in violence and the like. It has four kinds: himsananda (delight in violence), chauryananda (delight in theft), mrishananda (delight in falsehood), and parigrahananda (delight in possessiveness).

t: ** What is dharma-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is dharma-dhyana?
: Meditation imbued with dharma (righteousness) is called dharma-dhyana. It has four kinds: 1. ajna-vichaya, 2. apaya-vichaya, 3. vipaka-vichaya, 4. sansthana-vichaya.

t: ** What is ajna-vichaya dharma-dhyana, and what does it produce?

c.b: ** What is ajna-vichaya dharma-dhyana, and what does it produce?

: Reflecting that the scripture (agama) proclaimed by the omniscient is authoritative, and that it is exactly so and not otherwise, is ajna-vichaya dharma-dhyana. It assists firmness (nishtha) of conviction in the tattvas.

t: ** What is apaya-vichaya dharma-dhyana, and what does it produce?

c.b: ** What is apaya-vichaya dharma-dhyana, and what does it produce?
: Reflecting on how the wrong faith (mithya-darshan) of deluded beings may be removed. This produces detachment from the world and from sensual pleasures.

t: ** What is vipaka-vichaya dharma-dhyana, and what does it produce?

c.b: ** What is vipaka-vichaya dharma-dhyana, and what does it produce?
: Reflecting on the fruits (results) of karma. This produces knowledge of the diversity of karmic fruits and their causes.

t: ** What is sansthana-vichaya dharma-dhyana, and what does it produce?

c.b: ** What is sansthana-vichaya dharma-dhyana, and what does it produce?
: Reflecting on the arrangement of the three worlds. It has four kinds — pindastha, padastha, rupastha, rupatita. It firms up one's knowledge of the arrangement of the three worlds.

t: ** What is pindastha-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is pindastha-dhyana?
: Meditating on oneself by means of [prescribed] contemplations (dharanas) is pindastha-dhyana.

t: ** What is padastha-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is padastha-dhyana?
: Reflecting with the support of sacred mantras is padastha-dhyana.

t: ** What is rupastha-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is rupastha-dhyana?
: Meditating on the Arihanta and other Parameshthis (supreme beings) is rupastha-dhyana.

t: ** What is rupatita-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is rupatita-dhyana?
: Reflecting on the pure form of the soul is rupatita-dhyana.

t: ** What is shukla-dhyana?

c.b: ** What is shukla-dhyana?
: Pure meditation is called shukla-dhyana. It has four kinds: 1. prithaktva-vitarka, 2. ekatva-vitarka, 3. sukshma-kriya-pratipati, 4. vyuparata-kriya-nivartti.

t: ** What does prithaktva-vitarka shukla-dhyana produce? In which gunasthana does it occur?

c.b: ** What does prithaktva-vitarka shukla-dhyana produce? In which gunasthana does it occur?
: It produces the subsidence and destruction of mohaniya karma (deluding karma). It occurs from the eighth to the eleventh gunasthana.

t: ** What does ekatva-vitarka shukla-dhyana produce? In which gunasthana does it occur?

c.b: ** What does ekatva-vitarka shukla-dhyana produce? In which gunasthana does it occur?
: It produces the destruction of jnanavarana, darshanavarana and antaraya karmas. It occurs in the twelfth gunasthana.

t: ** What does sukshma-kriya-pratipati shukla-dhyana produce?

c.b: ** What does sukshma-kriya-pratipati shukla-dhyana produce?
: It produces the cessation of the yogas (activities), and it occurs in the thirteenth gunasthana.

t: ** What does vyuparata-kriya-nivritti shukla-dhyana produce?

c.b: ** What does vyuparata-kriya-nivritti shukla-dhyana produce?
: It produces the end of samsara, freedom from the body, and the attainment of moksha; it occurs in the fourteenth gunasthana.

t: ** From which to which gunasthana does arta-dhyana occur?

c.b: ** From which to which gunasthana does arta-dhyana occur?
: From the first to the sixth gunasthana.

t: ** From which to which gunasthana does raudra-dhyana occur?

c.b: ** From which to which gunasthana does raudra-dhyana occur?
: From the first to the fifth gunasthana.

t: ** Up to which gunasthana does dharma-dhyana continue?

c.b: ** Up to which gunasthana does dharma-dhyana continue?
: From the fourth to the eighth gunasthana (according to another opinion, up to the tenth).

t: ** From which to which gunasthana does shukla-dhyana occur?

c.b: ** From which to which gunasthana does shukla-dhyana occur?
: From the eleventh to the fourteenth gunasthana (another opinion: from the eighth to the fourteenth).

t: ** What is bhava?

c.b: ** What is bhava?
: The disposition of the conscious being is called bhava. When qualities manifest upon the subsidence, etc., of their opposing karmas, they are called bhava.

t: ** What is the material cause (upadana-karana) of the bhavas? What are they called?

c.b: ** What is the material cause (upadana-karana) of the bhavas? What are they called?
: They occur only within the soul. They are called the soul's own intrinsic realities (nija-tattva).

t: ** How many mula-bhavas (root/basic dispositions) are there?

c.b: ** How many mula-bhavas (root/basic dispositions) are there?
: Five: aupashamika (subsidential), kshayika (destructional), kshayopashamika (destructional-cum-subsidential), audayika (operative), parinamika (natural/innate).

t: ** What is aupashamika bhava? How many kinds are there? Name them.

c.b: ** What is aupashamika bhava? How many kinds are there? Name them.
: The qualities that manifest when their opposing karmas subside are called aupashamika bhava. It has two kinds — aupashamika-samyaktva, aupashamika-charitra.

t: ** What is aupashamika-samyaktva? How many kinds does it have?

c.b: ** What is aupashamika-samyaktva? How many kinds does it have?

: The samyaktva that occurs through the subsidence of the four anantanubandhi kashayas and the three darshana-mohaniya natures — these seven — is aupashamika-samyaktva. It has two kinds: prathamopashama-samyaktva (first subsidential right-faith), dvitiyopashama-samyaktva (second subsidential right-faith).

t: ** What is prathamopashama-samyaktva?

c.b: ** What is prathamopashama-samyaktva?
: The subsidential-samyaktva that occurs immediately after mithyatva (wrong faith) is called prathamopashama-samyaktva.

t: ** What is dvitiyopashama-samyaktva?

c.b: ** What is dvitiyopashama-samyaktva?
: The subsidential-samyaktva that occurs immediately after kshayopashamika-samyaktva is called dvitiyopashama-samyaktva.

t: ** What is aupashamika charitra (subsidential conduct)?

c.b: ** What is aupashamika charitra (subsidential conduct)?
: The conduct that occurs through the subsidence of the 21 natures of charitra-mohaniya (conduct-deluding karma).

t: ** What is kshayika bhava?

c.b: ** What is kshayika bhava?
: The qualities that manifest through the total (complete) destruction of their opposing karmas.

t: ** How many kinds of kshayika bhava are there? What are they?

c.b: ** How many kinds of kshayika bhava are there? What are they?

: There are 9 kinds: 1. kshayika-jnana (knowledge), 2. kshayika-darshan (perception), 3. kshayika-dana (giving), 4. kshayika-labha (gain), 5. kshayika-bhoga (one-time enjoyment), 6. kshayika-upabhoga (repeated enjoyment), 7. kshayika-virya (energy), 8. kshayika-samyaktva (right faith), 9. kshayika-charitra (conduct).

t: ** What is kshayopashamika bhava? How many are there? Name them.

c.b: ** What is kshayopashamika bhava? How many are there? Name them.

: The dispositions that manifest through the operative-destruction (udayabhavi-kshaya) of the completely-obscuring (sarvaghati) portions of one's opposing karmas, together with the subsidence-in-potential-existence of those same portions, and the rise of the partially-obscuring (deshaghati) portions, are called kshayopashamika bhava. There are eighteen of these: four kinds of jnana (knowledge), three kinds of ajnana (wrong knowledge), three kinds of darshan (perception), five labdhis (attainments), kshayopashamika-samyaktva, kshayopashamika-charitra, and samyamasamyam (partial restraint).

t: ** What is audayika bhava?

c.b: ** What is audayika bhava?

: The bearing of fruit by karmas, owing to the occasioning factors of dravya (substance), kshetra (place), kala (time) and bhava (disposition), is called udaya (rise/fruition). Dispositions occasioned by such rise are called audayika bhava.

t: ** How many kinds of audayika bhava are there? Name them.

c.b: ** How many kinds of audayika bhava are there? Name them.

: There are 21: 4 gatis (destinies), 4 kashayas (passions), 3 lingas (genders), 6 leshyas (thought-colourations), mithya-darshan (wrong faith), ajnana (wrong knowledge), asamyam (lack of restraint), asiddhatva (state of non-liberation).

t: ** What is parinamika bhava? How many are there?

c.b: ** What is parinamika bhava? How many are there?

: The dispositions that occur purely by the intrinsic nature of jiva-dravya, without dependence on the rise, subsidence, destruction or destruction-cum-subsidence of karmas, are parinamika bhava. There are three: jivatva (soul-hood), bhavyatva (fitness for liberation), abhavyatva (unfitness for liberation).

t: ** How many bhavas occur in the mithyatva (first) gunasthana? Name them.

c.b: ** How many bhavas occur in the mithyatva (first) gunasthana? Name them.
: 34. Ten of kshayopashamika, 21 of audayika, and 3 of parinamika.

t: ** How many bhavas occur in the second and third gunasthanas?

c.b: ** How many bhavas occur in the second and third gunasthanas?
: 32 bhavas — ten of kshayopashamika, 20 of audayika (excluding mithya-darshan), and, of parinamika, jivatva and bhavyatva.

t: ** How many bhavas occur in the fourth gunasthana? Which ones?

c.b: ** How many bhavas occur in the fourth gunasthana? Which ones?
: 23 bhavas — 2 of aupashamika, 2 of kshayika, 12 of kshayopashamika, 5 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika.

t: ** How many bhavas occur in the fifth gunasthana? Which ones?

c.b: ** How many bhavas occur in the fifth gunasthana? Which ones?
: 31 bhavas — upashama-samyaktva, kshayika-samyaktva, 13 of kshayopashamika, 14 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika.

t: ** Which bhavas occur in the sixth and seventh gunasthanas?

c.b: ** Which bhavas occur in the sixth and seventh gunasthanas?
: Upashama-samyaktva, kshayika-samyaktva, 14 of kshayopashamika, 13 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika — 31 bhavas in all.

t: ** How many bhavas occur in the eighth and ninth gunasthanas? Name them.

c.b: ** How many bhavas occur in the eighth and ninth gunasthanas? Name them.
: 29 bhavas — upashama-samyaktva, upashama-charitra, kshayika-samyaktva, kshayika-charitra, 12 of kshayopashamika, 11 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika.

t: ** Which bhavas occur in the tenth gunasthana?

c.b: ** Which bhavas occur in the tenth gunasthana?
: 23 bhavas — 2 of aupashamika, 2 of kshayika, 12 of kshayopashamika, 5 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika.

t: ** Which bhavas occur in the eleventh gunasthana?

c.b: ** Which bhavas occur in the eleventh gunasthana?
: 21 bhavas — 2 of aupashamika, 1 of kshayika-samyaktva, 12 of kshayopashamika, 4 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika.

t: ** Which bhavas occur in the twelfth gunasthana?

c.b: ** Which bhavas occur in the twelfth gunasthana?
: 20 bhavas — 2 of kshayika, 12 of kshayopashamika, 4 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika.

t: ** How many bhavas occur in the thirteenth gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many bhavas occur in the thirteenth gunasthana?
: 14 bhavas — 9 of kshayika, 3 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika.

t: ** How many bhavas occur in the fourteenth gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many bhavas occur in the fourteenth gunasthana?
: 13 bhavas — 9 of kshayika, 2 of audayika, and 2 of parinamika.

t: ** How many bhavas do the Siddhas (liberated souls) have?

c.b: ** How many bhavas do the Siddhas (liberated souls) have?
: 5 bhavas — kshayika-jnana, kshayika-darshan, kshayika-samyaktva, kshayika-virya, and jivatva.

t: ** What is gunasthana? How many are there? Name them.

c.b: ** What is gunasthana? How many are there? Name them.

: The particular gradational states of the soul's qualities of right faith (samyagdarshan), right knowledge (samyagjnana) and right conduct (samyakcharitra) — states occasioned by moha (delusion) and yoga (activity) — are called gunasthanas. There are fourteen of these: (1) mithyatva, (2) sasadana, (3) mishra, (4) avirata, (5) desha-samyama, (6) pramatta-virata, (7) apramatta-virata, (8) apurvakarana, (9) anivrittikarana, (10) sukshma-samparaya, (11) upashanta-moha, (12) kshina-moha, (13) sayoga-kevali, (14) ayoga-kevali.

t: ** The first four gunasthanas are occasioned by what?

c.b: ** The first four gunasthanas are occasioned by what?
: By darshana-moha (faith-deluding karma).

t: ** The fifth to the twelfth gunasthanas are occasioned by what?

c.b: ** The fifth to the twelfth gunasthanas are occasioned by what?
: By charitra-moha (conduct-deluding karma).

t: ** The thirteenth and fourteenth gunasthanas are occasioned by what?

c.b: ** The thirteenth and fourteenth gunasthanas are occasioned by what?
: By yoga (activity).

t: ** What is mithyatva (the first gunasthana)?

c.b: ** What is mithyatva (the first gunasthana)?
: The particular state of the soul characterised by lack of faith in the true realities (tattvas), arising from the rise of mithyatva-prakriti (wrong-faith karma), is called mithyatva.

t: ** What is sasadana (the second gunasthana)?

c.b: ** What is sasadana (the second gunasthana)?

: During the period of prathamopashama-samyaktva, when at least one instant and at most six avalis remain, the state devoid of samyaktva that occurs through the rise of any one anantanubandhi-kashaya is called the sasadana gunasthana.

t: ** What is the mishra (third) gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is the mishra (third) gunasthana?

: Through the rise of samyagmithyatva-prakriti, when a soul's disposition is neither purely of the nature of samyaktva nor purely of the nature of mithyatva, but a mixture of both, this is called the mishra gunasthana.

t: ** What is avirata-samyaktva (the fourth gunasthana)?

c.b: ** What is avirata-samyaktva (the fourth gunasthana)?
: Where samyagdarshan (right faith) has arisen but, owing to the rise of apratyakhyanavarana kashaya, the vow of renouncing the five sins has not yet been taken, this is called avirata-samyaktva.

t: ** What is desha-samyata (the fifth gunasthana)?

c.b: ** What is desha-samyata (the fifth gunasthana)?

: The particular disposition of the soul in which, through the non-rise of apratyakhyanavarana kashaya, there is restraint (samyam) in the form of renouncing violence against trasa (mobile) beings, but, through the rise of pratyakhyanavarana kashaya, violence against sthavara (immobile) beings is not renounced — remaining in the form of asamyam (partial non-restraint) — is called the desha-samyata gunasthana.

t: ** What is the pramatta-virata (sixth) gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is the pramatta-virata (sixth) gunasthana?
: The state of restraint (samyam) accompanied by carelessness (pramada), arising through the intense rise of sanjvalana kashaya and the no-kashayas, is called pramatta-virata.

t: ** What is the apramatta-virata (seventh) gunasthana? How many kinds does it have?

c.b: ** What is the apramatta-virata (seventh) gunasthana? How many kinds does it have?

: The state of restraint free from carelessness, arising through the mild rise of sanjvalana kashaya and no-kashayas, is called apramatta-virata gunasthana. It has two kinds: svasthana-apramatta-virata and satishaya-apramatta-virata.

t: ** What is svasthana-apramatta-virata gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is svasthana-apramatta-virata gunasthana?
: The disposition in which a soul continuously moves back and forth between the sixth and the seventh gunasthanas.

t: ** What is satishaya-apramatta-virata?

c.b: ** What is satishaya-apramatta-virata?
: That state in which a soul is on the verge of ascending the shreni (the ladder of spiritual purification).

t: ** What is shreni (the ladder/ascending scale)?

c.b: ** What is shreni (the ladder/ascending scale)?
: The sequential subsidence or destruction of the 21 natures of charitra-mohaniya karma is called shreni.

t: ** Which gunasthanas belong to the upashama-shreni (subsidential ladder) and the kshapaka-shreni (destructive ladder)?

c.b: ** Which gunasthanas belong to the upashama-shreni (subsidential ladder) and the kshapaka-shreni (destructive ladder)?
: The upashama-shreni comprises gunasthanas 8, 9, 10 and 11; the kshapaka-shreni comprises gunasthanas 8, 9, 10 and 12.

t: ** What is the apurvakarana (eighth) gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is the apurvakarana (eighth) gunasthana?

: That state in which the soul's disposition, from moment to moment, keeps taking on ever-newer (apurva) forms — that is, souls existing at different instants always have dissimilar dispositions, while souls existing at the same instant may have dispositions that are similar or dissimilar — is called apurvakarana.

t: ** What is the anivrittikarana (ninth) gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is the anivrittikarana (ninth) gunasthana?
: That state in which souls existing at different instants always have dissimilar dispositions, while souls existing at the very same instant have exactly similar dispositions.

t: ** What is the sukshma-samparaya (tenth) gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is the sukshma-samparaya (tenth) gunasthana?
: The disposition of a soul experiencing the rise of extremely subtle lobha-kashaya (greed) alone is called the sukshma-samparaya gunasthana.

t: ** What is upashanta-moha (the eleventh gunasthana)?

c.b: ** What is upashanta-moha (the eleventh gunasthana)?
: The disposition accompanied by yathakhyata-charitra (ideal conduct) that occurs through the subsidence of all 21 natures of charitra-mohaniya karma is called upashanta-moha.

t: ** What is the kshina-moha (twelfth) gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is the kshina-moha (twelfth) gunasthana?
: The disposition accompanied by an utterly flawless yathakhyata-charitra, occurring through the destruction of mohaniya karma, is called kshina-moha.

t: ** What is the sayoga-kevali (thirteenth) gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is the sayoga-kevali (thirteenth) gunasthana?
: The disposition, free of the four ghatiya (destructive) karmas and endowed with kevala-jnana (omniscience) and yoga (activity), is called sayoga-kevali.

t: ** What is the ayoga-kevali (fourteenth) gunasthana?

c.b: ** What is the ayoga-kevali (fourteenth) gunasthana?
: The disposition free of ghatiya karmas and of yoga, and endowed with the ananta-chatushtaya (the four infinite qualities), is called ayoga-kevali gunasthana.

t: ** How many gunasthanas occur in deva-gati (celestial existence) and naraka-gati (hell existence)?

c.b: ** How many gunasthanas occur in deva-gati (celestial existence) and naraka-gati (hell existence)?
: Gunasthanas one to four.

t: ** How many gunasthanas occur in tiryancha-gati (animal/plant existence)?

c.b: ** How many gunasthanas occur in tiryancha-gati (animal/plant existence)?
: Gunasthanas one to five.

t: ** How many gunasthanas occur in manushya-gati (human existence)?

c.b: ** How many gunasthanas occur in manushya-gati (human existence)?
: All fourteen, from one to fourteen.

t: ** Which gunasthana applies to beings from ekendriya (one-sensed) up to asamjni-panchendriya (mindless five-sensed)?

c.b: ** Which gunasthana applies to beings from ekendriya (one-sensed) up to asamjni-panchendriya (mindless five-sensed)?
: The mithyatva gunasthana. (According to another opinion, sasadana also occurs in them during the aparyapta [undeveloped] state.)

t: ** Up to which gunasthana does asamyam (lack of restraint) occur?

c.b: ** Up to which gunasthana does asamyam (lack of restraint) occur?
: Up to the fourth gunasthana.

t: ** Up to which gunasthana do pramada (carelessness) and deliberate attachment occur?

c.b: ** Up to which gunasthana do pramada (carelessness) and deliberate attachment occur?
: Up to the sixth gunasthana.

t: ** Up to which gunasthana does kashaya (passion) occur?

c.b: ** Up to which gunasthana does kashaya (passion) occur?
: Up to the tenth gunasthana.

t: ** Up to which gunasthana do yoga and the operation (udaya) of the body [-determining karma] occur?

c.b: ** Up to which gunasthana do yoga and the operation (udaya) of the body [-determining karma] occur?
: Up to the thirteenth gunasthana.

t: ** Up to which gunasthana does veda (sex-disposition) occur?

c.b: ** Up to which gunasthana does veda (sex-disposition) occur?
: All three psychic genders (bhava-veda) last up to the ninth gunasthana.

t: ** How many yogas occur in the first and second gunasthanas?

c.b: ** How many yogas occur in the first and second gunasthanas?
: Thirteen yogas — all except aharaka and aharaka-mishra.

t: ** How many yogas occur in the third gunasthana? Which ones?

c.b: ** How many yogas occur in the third gunasthana? Which ones?
: 10 yogas — the four mental, the four vocal, and the audarika and vaikriyika bodily yogas.

t: ** How many yogas occur in the fifth gunasthana and from the seventh up to the twelfth gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many yogas occur in the fifth gunasthana and from the seventh up to the twelfth gunasthana?
: Nine yogas — the four mental, the four vocal, and the audarika bodily yoga.

t: ** How many yogas occur in the sixth gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many yogas occur in the sixth gunasthana?
: Eleven yogas in the sixth gunasthana — the four mental, the four vocal, and the audarika, aharaka and aharaka-mishra bodily yogas.

t: ** How many yogas occur in the thirteenth gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many yogas occur in the thirteenth gunasthana?
: Seven — true-mental, neither-true-nor-untrue-mental, true-vocal, neither-true-nor-untrue-vocal, audarika, audarika-mishra, and karmana yoga.

t: ** How long is the duration (kala) of the first gunasthana?

c.b: ** How long is the duration (kala) of the first gunasthana?
: Anadi-anant (beginningless-and-endless), anadi-sant (beginningless-but-with-an-end), or sadi-sant (with-a-beginning-and-with-an-end) — of three kinds.

t: ** With respect to whom is [this duration] anādi-anant (beginningless-and-endless)?

c.b: ** With respect to whom is [this duration] anādi-anant (beginningless-and-endless)?
: With respect to the abhavya (a soul incapable of ever attaining liberation).

t: ** With respect to whom is it anādi-sānt (beginningless-but-with-an-end)?

c.b: ** With respect to whom is it anādi-sānt (beginningless-but-with-an-end)?
: With respect to the bhavya jīva (a soul capable of liberation, prior to attaining right faith).

t: ** With respect to whom is it sādi-sānt (with-a-beginning-and-with-an-end)?

c.b: ** With respect to whom is it sādi-sānt (with-a-beginning-and-with-an-end)?
: With respect to one who, having attained samyagdarśana (right faith), again falls back into mithyādṛṣṭi (wrong faith, the first gunasthana).

t: ** What are the minimum (jaghanya) and maximum (utkṛṣṭa) durations of the second gunasthana?

c.b: ** What are the minimum (jaghanya) and maximum (utkṛṣṭa) durations of the second gunasthana?
: The minimum duration is one samaya (instant); the maximum duration is six āvalīs.

t: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the third gunasthana?

c.b: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the third gunasthana?
: Antarmuhūrta (both).

t: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the fourth gunasthana?

c.b: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the fourth gunasthana?
: The minimum duration is antarmuhūrta, and the maximum duration is a little less than one koṭipūrva plus thirty-three sāgaras (sāgaropama).

t: ** What are the maximum and minimum durations of the fifth gunasthana?

c.b: ** What are the maximum and minimum durations of the fifth gunasthana?

: The minimum duration is antarmuhūrta, and the maximum duration is one koṭipūrva minus an antarmuhūrta. A sammūrchhana (spontaneously-generated) tiryañca (animal) can attain saṃyamāsaṃyama (partial self-restraint, the fifth gunasthana) together with vedaka-samyaktva an antarmuhūrta after birth. With respect to human beings, it is one koṭipūrva minus eight years.

t: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the sixth and seventh gunasthanas?

c.b: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the sixth and seventh gunasthanas?
: For both gunasthanas, with respect to death, the minimum duration is one samaya, and the maximum duration is antarmuhūrta.

t: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the kṣapaka-śreṇī (the ladder of annihilation of karmas)?

c.b: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the kṣapaka-śreṇī (the ladder of annihilation of karmas)?
: Antarmuhūrta (both).

t: [as printed].** What are the minimum and maximum durations for all four stages of the upaśamaka (suppressing) souls?

c.b: [as printed].** What are the minimum and maximum durations for all four stages of the upaśamaka (suppressing) souls?
: With respect to death, the minimum duration is one samaya, and the maximum duration is antarmuhūrta.

t: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the thirteenth gunasthana?

c.b: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the thirteenth gunasthana?
: The minimum duration is antarmuhūrta, and the maximum duration is eight years plus a koṭipūrva year minus eight antarmuhūrtas.

t: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the ayogakevalī gunasthana (fourteenth)?

c.b: ** What are the minimum and maximum durations of the ayogakevalī gunasthana (fourteenth)?
: Both the minimum and the maximum duration are antarmuhūrta.

t: ** How many souls are there in the first gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many souls are there in the first gunasthana?
: Anantānanta (infinite-times-infinite) souls.

t: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the second gunasthana?

c.b: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the second gunasthana?
: 52 crore, with respect to human beings.

t: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the third gunasthana?

c.b: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the third gunasthana?
: 104 crore souls.

t: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the fourth gunasthana?

c.b: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the fourth gunasthana?
: 700 crore.

t: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the fifth gunasthana?

c.b: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the fifth gunasthana?
: 13 crore souls.

t: ** How many souls are there in the sixth gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many souls are there in the sixth gunasthana?
: 59,398,206 — five crore ninety-three lakh ninety-eight thousand two hundred six.

t: ** How many souls are there in the seventh gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many souls are there in the seventh gunasthana?
: 29,699,103 — two crore ninety-six lakh ninety-nine thousand one hundred three souls.

t: ** How many souls are there in the thirteenth gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many souls are there in the thirteenth gunasthana?
: 898,502 — eight lakh ninety-eight thousand five hundred two souls.

t: ** How many souls are there in the fourteenth gunasthana?

c.b: ** How many souls are there in the fourteenth gunasthana?
: 598 souls.

t: ** In the second, third, fourth, and fifth gunasthanas, with respect to each of the four gatis (realms of existence) separately, how many souls are there?

c.b: ** In the second, third, fourth, and fifth gunasthanas, with respect to each of the four gatis (realms of existence) separately, how many souls are there?
: In each of the four gunasthanas, separately, they number an innumerable part (asaṅkhyātavāṅ bhāga) of a palya (a unit of numerical measure).

t: ** Among those ascending the upaśama-śreṇī (ladder of suppression), how many souls are there in each separate gunasthana?

c.b: ** Among those ascending the upaśama-śreṇī (ladder of suppression), how many souls are there in each separate gunasthana?
: In each of the four gunasthanas separately, there are 299.

t: ** For those on the kṣapaka-śreṇī, what is the separate number of souls in each of the four gunasthanas?

c.b: ** For those on the kṣapaka-śreṇī, what is the separate number of souls in each of the four gunasthanas?
: In each of the four, separately, there are 598.

t: ** In all four gunasthanas of the upaśama-śreṇī together, how many souls are there in total?

c.b: ** In all four gunasthanas of the upaśama-śreṇī together, how many souls are there in total?
: In all four stages of the upaśama-śreṇī together, there are 1196 souls.

t: ** In the four gunasthanas of the kṣapaka-śreṇī, how many souls are there?

c.b: ** In the four gunasthanas of the kṣapaka-śreṇī, how many souls are there?
: In all four stages of the kṣapaka-śreṇī together, there are 2392 souls.

t: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the first gunasthana?

c.b: ** With respect to human beings, how many souls are in the first gunasthana?
: They number an innumerable part of the jagat-śreṇī (a cosmological linear measure).

t: ** From the sixth to the fourteenth gunasthana, how many munirājas (great ascetic-monks) are there altogether?

c.b: ** From the sixth to the fourteenth gunasthana, how many munirājas (great ascetic-monks) are there altogether?
: There are nine crore minus three (i.e. 89,999,997) munirājas. All of these are bhāvaliṅgī (true ascetics by inner disposition, not merely outward form).

t: ** What is called karma?

c.b: ** What is called karma?
: Karma is the bonding of karmic pudgala-varganas (material karmic particle-groups) with the soul, occasioned by the soul's own psychic states such as rāga (attachment) and the like.

t: ** How many kinds of karma are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of karma are there?
: Karma has divisions of 2, 3, 4, 8, 148, and, ultimately, a number equal to innumerable lokas.

t: ** What are the three kinds of karma?

c.b: ** What are the three kinds of karma?
: Dravya-karma (material karma), bhāva-karma (psychic karma), and no-karma (quasi-karma).

t: ** What is called dravya-karma?

c.b: ** What is called dravya-karma?
: The mass of karmic pudgala [matter] such as jñānāvaraṇa and the rest.

t: ** What is called bhāva-karma?

c.b: ** What is called bhāva-karma?
: Psychic states such as rāga (attachment) and dveṣa (aversion).

t: ** What is called no-karma?

c.b: ** What is called no-karma?
: External instrumental causes such as the body.

t: ** How many divisions does dravya-karma have?

c.b: ** How many divisions does dravya-karma have?

: Eight: jñānāvaraṇa (knowledge-obscuring), darśanāvaraṇa (perception-obscuring), vedanīya (feeling-producing), mohanīya (deluding), āyu (life-span-determining), nāma (body-determining), gotra (status-determining), and antarāya (obstructing).

t: ** What are the two divisions of dravya-karma?

c.b: ** What are the two divisions of dravya-karma?
: Ghātiyā (destructive) and aghātiyā (non-destructive).

t: ** What is called ghātiyā karma?

c.b: ** What is called ghātiyā karma?
: That which harms the soul's essential (anujīvī) qualities such as jñāna (knowledge), darśana (perception), vīrya (energy), samyaktva (right faith), and so on, is called ghātiyā karma.

t: ** Which karmas are ghātiyā?

c.b: ** Which karmas are ghātiyā?
: Jñānāvaraṇa, darśanāvaraṇa, mohanīya, and antarāya.

t: ** What is called aghātiyā karma, and which are they?

c.b: ** What is called aghātiyā karma, and which are they?
: That which harms the soul's incidental (pratijīvī) qualities is called aghātiyā karma: āyu, nāma, gotra, and vedanīya.

t: ** How many kinds of bandha (bonding) are there, and what are they?

c.b: ** How many kinds of bandha (bonding) are there, and what are they?
: Four kinds: prakṛti-bandha (nature-bonding), pradeśa-bandha (quantity-bonding), sthiti-bandha (duration-bonding), and anubhāga-bandha (intensity-bonding).

t: ** What is called prakṛti-bandha?

c.b: ** What is called prakṛti-bandha?
: The specific relationship of adhesion (saṃśleṣa) of material karmas with the soul is called prakṛti-bandha.

t: ** What is called pradeśa-bandha?

c.b: ** What is called pradeśa-bandha?
: The measure of how much quantity of karmic pudgala-varganas has come into bondage — that measure is called pradeśa-bandha.

t: ** What is called sthiti-bandha?

c.b: ** What is called sthiti-bandha?
: The length of time for which karma remains bound with the soul.

t: ** What is called anubhāga-bandha?

c.b: ** What is called anubhāga-bandha?
: The potency of karmas in yielding their fruit is called anubhāga-bandha.

t: ** How many divisions does ghātiyā karma have?

c.b: ** How many divisions does ghātiyā karma have?
: Two: sarvaghāti (totally obscuring) and deśaghāti (partially obscuring).

t: ** Which are the sarvaghāti (totally obscuring) natures (prakṛtis)? Name them.

c.b: ** Which are the sarvaghāti (totally obscuring) natures (prakṛtis)? Name them.

: Kevala-jñānāvaraṇa, kevala-darśanāvaraṇa, the five [kinds of] nidrā (sleep), the four anantānubandhī [passions], the four apratyākhyāna [passions], the four pratyākhyāna [passions], and mithyātva, samyagmithyātva — 21 natures are sarvaghāti.

t: ** Which are the deśaghāti (partially obscuring) natures? Name them.

c.b: ** Which are the deśaghāti (partially obscuring) natures? Name them.

: The [remaining] four of jñānāvaraṇa, three of darśanāvaraṇa, the four saṃjvalana (smouldering) passions, the nine no-kaṣāyas (quasi-passions) beginning with laughter, five of antarāya, and the samyaktva-prakṛti — thus 26 natures are deśaghāti.

t: ** What are the divisions of jñānāvaraṇa karma?

c.b: ** What are the divisions of jñānāvaraṇa karma?

: Mati-jñānāvaraṇa, śruta-jñānāvaraṇa, avadhi-jñānāvaraṇa, manaḥparyaya-jñānāvaraṇa, and kevala-jñānāvaraṇa (obscuring sensory, scriptural, clairvoyant, telepathic, and omniscient knowledge respectively).

t: ** What are the divisions of darśanāvaraṇa karma?

c.b: ** What are the divisions of darśanāvaraṇa karma?

: Cakṣu-darśanāvaraṇa, acakṣu-darśanāvaraṇa, avadhi-darśanāvaraṇa, kevala-darśanāvaraṇa (obscuring ocular, non-ocular, clairvoyant, and omniscient perception); and nidrā, nidrā-nidrā, pracalā, pracalā-pracalā, styānagṛddhi (the five degrees of sleep/torpor).

t: ** What are the divisions of vedanīya karma?

c.b: ** What are the divisions of vedanīya karma?
: Sātā-vedanīya (pleasure-producing) and asātā-vedanīya (pain-producing).

t: ** How many divisions does mohanīya karma have?

c.b: ** How many divisions does mohanīya karma have?
: Darśana-mohanīya (faith-deluding) and cāritra-mohanīya (conduct-deluding).

t: ** How many divisions does darśana-mohanīya have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many divisions does darśana-mohanīya have? Name them.
: Three: mithyātva, samyagmithyātva, and samyaktva-prakṛti.

t: ** How many divisions does cāritra-mohanīya have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many divisions does cāritra-mohanīya have? Name them.
: Cāritra-mohanīya has two divisions: kaṣāya-vedanīya (relating to the passions) and akaṣāya-vedanīya (relating to the quasi-passions).

t: ** How many divisions does kaṣāya-vedanīya have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many divisions does kaṣāya-vedanīya have? Name them.
: Sixteen: four anantānubandhī, four apratyākhyāna, four pratyākhyāna, four saṃjvalana — [each set of four being] krodha (anger), māna (pride), māyā (deceit), lobha (greed).

t: ** How many divisions does akaṣāya-vedanīya have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many divisions does akaṣāya-vedanīya have? Name them.

: Nine: hāsya (laughter), rati (liking), arati (disliking), śoka (sorrow), bhaya (fear), jugupsā (disgust), puruṣa-veda (male sex-passion), strī-veda (female sex-passion), napuṃsaka-veda (neuter sex-passion).

t: ** How many divisions does āyu-karma have?

c.b: ** How many divisions does āyu-karma have?
: Four: naraka-āyu (hellish life-span), tiryañca-āyu (animal/plant life-span), manuṣya-āyu (human life-span), deva-āyu (celestial life-span).

t: ** How many divisions does nāma-karma have?

c.b: ** How many divisions does nāma-karma have?

: 93: gati (destiny) 4, jāti (class of being) 5, śarīra (body) 5, aṅgopāṅga (limbs/minor limbs) 3, bandhana (bonding) 5, saṅghāta (consolidation) 5, saṃsthāna (shape) 6, saṃhanana (bone-joint structure) 6, sparśa (touch) 8, rasa (taste) 5, gandha (smell) 2, varṇa (colour) 5 (these twenty together called sparśādika), ānupūrvī (migratory-form) 4, vihāyogati (gait) 2; and sūkṣma (subtle), sādhāraṇa (common-bodied), aparyāpta (undeveloped), durbhaga (unfortunate), duḥsvara (harsh-voiced), anādeya (unimposing), aśubha (inauspicious), asthira (unstable), ayaśaskīrti (ill-famed), sthāvara (immobile) — together with the ten opposites of these; and nirmāṇa (organization), agurulaghu (neither-heavy-nor-light), ucchvāsa (respiration), upaghāta (self-injury), paraghāta (injuring-others capacity), ātapa (heat-radiating body), udyota (cool-light-radiating body), and tīrthaṅkara (the Tīrthaṅkara-making nature).

t: ** How many divisions does antarāya-karma have? Name them.

c.b: ** How many divisions does antarāya-karma have? Name them.

: Five: dānāntarāya (obstructing charity), lābhāntarāya (obstructing gain), bhogāntarāya (obstructing one-time enjoyment), upabhogāntarāya (obstructing repeated enjoyment), vīryāntarāya (obstructing energy).

t: ** How many sub-divisions (uttara-bheda) do the karmas have?

c.b: ** How many sub-divisions (uttara-bheda) do the karmas have?
: 148 divisions.

t: ** From the standpoint of non-differentiation (abheda-vivakṣā), how many bandha-prakṛtis (bonding-natures) are there?

c.b: ** From the standpoint of non-differentiation (abheda-vivakṣā), how many bandha-prakṛtis (bonding-natures) are there?

: There are 120 bandha-prakṛtis. Within darśana-mohanīya, bonding occurs only through mithyātva — the other two [samyagmithyātva and samyaktva-prakṛti] are merely fragments of it, so [the three] are counted as one. In nāma-karma, the 5 bandhana and 5 saṅghāta — these 10 natures — are subsumed within the 5 śarīra categories; and among varṇa and the rest [touch, taste, smell, colour], bonding occurs for only 4 [representative types].

t: ** How many kinds of aghātiyā karma are there?

c.b: ** How many kinds of aghātiyā karma are there?
: Two kinds: praśasta (auspicious, puṇya) and apraśasta (inauspicious, pāpa).

t: ** How many praśasta (auspicious) natures are there? Which are they?

c.b: ** How many praśasta (auspicious) natures are there? Which are they?
: 68: sātā-vedanīya, tiryañca-āyu, manuṣya-āyu, deva-āyu, ucca-gotra (high status), and 63 of nāma-karma.

t: ** Which are the 63 praśasta (puṇya) natures of nāma-karma?

c.b: ** Which are the 63 praśasta (puṇya) natures of nāma-karma?

: Varṇādi (colour-group) 20, trasādi (mobile-being group) 12, śarīra 5, bandhana 5, saṅghāta 5, aṅgopāṅga 3, the agurulaghu-ṣaṭka (sixfold agurulaghu group) minus upaghāta (5), and manuṣya-gati, manuṣya-gatyānupūrvī, deva-gati, deva-gatyānupūrvī, pañcendriya-jāti, samacatuḥ-saṃsthāna (symmetrical shape), vajra-vṛṣabha-nārāca-saṃhanana (adamantine skeletal structure), and praśasta-vihāyogati (graceful gait).

t: ** What are the 20 of varṇādi?

c.b: ** What are the 20 of varṇādi?
: Varṇa (colour) 5, rasa (taste) 5, sparśa (touch) 8, gandha (smell) 2.

t: ** Which is the agurulaghu-ṣaṭka?

c.b: ** Which is the agurulaghu-ṣaṭka?
: Agurulaghu, upaghāta, paraghāta, ucchvāsa, ātapa, udyota.

t: ** What are the 12 of the trasa group?

c.b: ** What are the 12 of the trasa group?

: Trasa (mobile), bādara (gross), paryāpta (fully developed), pratyeka-śarīra (individual body), sthira (stable), śubha (auspicious), subhaga (fortunate), susvara (sweet-voiced), ādeya (impressive), yaśaḥkīrti (fame), nirmāṇa, tīrthaṅkara.

t: ** Which are the apraśasta (inauspicious) natures, and how many are there?

c.b: ** Which are the apraśasta (inauspicious) natures, and how many are there?
: 47 of ghātiyā karma, asātā-vedanīya, nīca-gotra (low status), naraka-āyu, and 50 of nāma-karma — 100 apraśasta (pāpa) natures in all.

t: ** Which are the 50 apraśasta natures of nāma-karma?

c.b: ** Which are the 50 apraśasta natures of nāma-karma?

: Varṇādi 20, saṃsthāna 5, saṃhanana 5, jāti 4, sthāvara-daśaka (the tenfold immobile group) 10, naraka-gati, naraka-gatyānupūrvī, tiryañca-gati, tiryañca-gatyānupūrvī, upaghāta, and apraśasta-vihāyogati.

t: ** What is the sthāvara-daśaka?

c.b: ** What is the sthāvara-daśaka?
: Sthāvara, sūkṣma, sādhāraṇa, aparyāpta, asthira, aśubha, durbhaga, duḥsvara, anādeya, ayaśaskīrti.

t: ** How many karaṇas (operations/processes) pertaining to karma are there?

c.b: ** How many karaṇas (operations/processes) pertaining to karma are there?

: Ten: 1. Bandha (bonding), 2. Udaya (fruition), 3. Sattva (continued existence), 4. Utkarṣaṇa (enhancement), 5. Apakarṣaṇa (diminution), 6. Saṅkramaṇa (transformation into a same-class nature), 7. Udīraṇā (premature fruition), 8. Upaśama (suppression), 9. Nidhatti (fixation), 10. Nikācita (total fixation).

t: ** What is called bandha-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called bandha-karaṇa?
: Karmas entering a relationship of occupying the same space-points (ekakṣetrāvagāha) with the soul is called bandha.

t: ** What is called udaya-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called udaya-karaṇa?
: A karma reaching its own [allotted] duration, that is, the time for yielding its fruit having arrived, is called udaya.

t: ** What is called sattva-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called sattva-karaṇa?
: The continued existence of karmic pudgala-varganas in the form of bound karma is called sattva.

t: ** What is called utkarṣaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called utkarṣaṇa?
: The increase of the duration and intensity of karmas is utkarṣaṇa.

t: ** What is called apakarṣaṇa-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called apakarṣaṇa-karaṇa?
: The decrease of the duration and intensity of karmas is apakarṣaṇa.

t: ** What is called saṅkramaṇa-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called saṅkramaṇa-karaṇa?
: A karmic nature transforming into a nature of the same class (sajāti) is called saṅkramaṇa.

t: ** What is called udīraṇā-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called udīraṇā-karaṇa?
: Bringing forward into the udaya-āvalī (the fruition-line), by the force of apakarṣaṇa, a karma whose time of fruition has not yet arrived, is udīraṇā.

t: ** What is called upaśama-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called upaśama-karaṇa?
: The state in which a karma is not brought into the udaya-āvalī, i.e., does not reach the condition of udīraṇā, is upaśama.

t: ** What is called nidhatti-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called nidhatti-karaṇa?
: A karma that does not undergo the states of udīraṇā and saṅkramaṇa is nidhatti.

t: ** What is called nikācita-karaṇa?

c.b: ** What is called nikācita-karaṇa?
: A karma that does not undergo the states of udīraṇā, saṅkramaṇa, utkarṣaṇa, and apakarṣaṇa is nikācita.

t: ** What is called bandha-vyucchitti (cessation of bonding)?

c.b: ** What is called bandha-vyucchitti (cessation of bonding)?

: Up through the gunasthana at which the bandha-vyucchitti of certain natures (prakṛtis) is said to occur, the bonding of those natures continues; in any gunasthana beyond that, no bonding of them occurs any longer — that is, saṃvara (stoppage) of those natures takes place.

t: ** In the mithyātva gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the mithyātva gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

: Sixteen: (1) mithyātva, (2) huṇḍaka-saṃsthāna (misshapen configuration), (3) napuṃsaka-veda, (4) asaṃprāptāsṛpāṭikā-saṃhanana (the loosest bone-joint structure), (5) ekendriya, (6) dvīndriya, (7) trīndriya, (8) caturindriya, (9) sthāvara, (10) ātapa, (11) sūkṣma, (12) sādhāraṇa, (13) aparyāpta, (14) naraka-gati, (15) naraka-gatyānupūrvī, (16) naraka-āyu.

t: ** In the sāsādana gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the sāsādana gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

: 25 natures: the four anantānubandhī [passions], 4 saṃhananas, 4 saṃsthānas, 3 nidrās, durbhaga, duḥsvara, anādeya, tiryañca-gatyānupūrvī, tiryañca-āyu, strī-veda, nīca-gotra, udyota, and apraśasta-vihāyogati.

t: ** In the asaṃyata gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the asaṃyata gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?
: 10 natures: manuṣya-gati, manuṣya-gatyānupūrvī, manuṣya-āyu, audārika-śarīra (gross physical body), audārika-aṅgopāṅga, vajra-vṛṣabha-nārāca-saṃhanana, and the four apratyākhyāna [passions].

t: ** In the deśasaṃyata gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the deśasaṃyata gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?
: Four: the four pratyākhyāna [passions].

t: ** In the pramatta gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the pramatta gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?
: Six: asthira, aśubha, ayaśaḥkīrti, asātā-vedanīya, arati, śoka.

t: ** In the apramatta gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the apramatta gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?
: One — deva-āyu.

t: ** In the apūrvakaraṇa gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the apūrvakaraṇa gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

: 36. In the first part [of this gunasthana]: nidrā and pracalā; in the sixth part: 30 of nāma-karma — tīrthaṅkara, nirmāṇa, praśasta-vihāyogati, pañcendriya-jāti, taijasa-śarīra, kārmaṇa-śarīra, āhāraka-śarīra, vaikriyika-śarīra, āhāraka-aṅgopāṅga, vaikriyika-aṅgopāṅga, sparśa, rasa, gandha, varṇa, agurulaghu, upaghāta, paraghāta, ucchvāsa, trasa, bādara, paryāpta, sthira, pratyeka-śarīra, śubha, susvara, subhaga, ādeya, deva-gati, deva-gatyānupūrvī, samacatuḥ-saṃsthāna; in the seventh part: hāsya, rati, bhaya, jugupsā.

t: ** In the anivṛttikaraṇa gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the anivṛttikaraṇa gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?
: 5. In the first part: puruṣa-veda; second part: saṃjvalana krodha; third part: saṃjvalana māna; fourth part: saṃjvalana māyā; fifth part: saṃjvalana lobha.

t: ** In the sūkṣmasāmparāya gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the sūkṣmasāmparāya gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?
: 16: 5 of jñānāvaraṇa, 4 of darśanāvaraṇa, 5 of antarāya, yaśaḥkīrti, ucca-gotra.

t: ** In the sayogakevalī gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?

c.b: ** In the sayogakevalī gunasthana, how many natures cease being bound?
: One — sātā-vedanīya.

t: ** What is called udaya-vyucchitti (cessation of fruition)?

c.b: ** What is called udaya-vyucchitti (cessation of fruition)?
: The fruition (udaya) of a nature continues only up through the gunasthana at which its udaya-vyucchitti is stated to occur; beyond that, it does not occur in any gunasthana.

t: ** In the mithyātva gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?

c.b: ** In the mithyātva gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?

: According to Ācārya Puṣpadanta and Bhūtabali, 10: mithyātva, ātapa, sūkṣma, sādhāraṇa, aparyāpta, sthāvara, ekendriya, and the vikalatraya (the two-, three-, and four-sensed classes). According to Ācārya Yativṛṣabhācārya, 5: mithyātva, ātapa, sūkṣma, sādhāraṇa, aparyāpta.

t: ** In the sāsādana gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?

c.b: ** In the sāsādana gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?
: According to Ācārya Puṣpadanta and Bhūtabali, the four anantānubandhī. According to Ācārya Yativṛṣabhācārya, 9: the four anantānubandhī, sthāvara, and the four jātis beginning with ekendriya.

t: ** In the miśra gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?

c.b: ** In the miśra gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?
: One — samyaktva-mithyātva (the mixed faith-nature).

t: ** In the asaṃyata gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?

c.b: ** In the asaṃyata gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?
: 17: the vaikriyika-aṣṭaka (eightfold vaikriyika group), the four apratyākhyāna passions, tiryañca-gatyānupūrvī, manuṣya-gatyānupūrvī, durbhaga, anādeya, ayaśaḥkīrti.

t: ** What is the vaikriyika-aṣṭaka? Name them.

c.b: ** What is the vaikriyika-aṣṭaka? Name them.
: Deva-gati, deva-gatyānupūrvī, naraka-gati, naraka-gatyānupūrvī, vaikriyika-śarīra, vaikriyika-aṅgopāṅga, naraka-āyu, deva-āyu.

t: ** In the deśasaṃyata gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?

c.b: ** In the deśasaṃyata gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?
: Eight: the four pratyākhyāna, tiryañca-gati, tiryañca-āyu, udyota, nīca-gotra.

t: ** In the pramatta gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?

c.b: ** In the pramatta gunasthana, how many natures cease fruition?
